magisterium.assessment_en: The passage mostly expresses Catholic emphases: the importance of the fear of God, the call to conversion, the proclamation of the Gospel, and the distinction between condemning sin and accepting the sinner. Nevertheless, the claim that a believer is "free from their ruin" if they have delivered a warning can be misunderstood as implying that man can judge another's guilt or salvation in advance, and the accusation of a widespread "lobby" remains unproven within the passage itself.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The biblical call to the fear of the Lord does not merely mean fear of punishment, but reverence before God that should go together with love; John Paul II explicitly emphasizes that fear and love must be held together. Jesus' proclamation includes both a call to conversion and the offer of forgiveness, so a warning about sin should not be separated from mercy and the hope of change. Paul's text in Romans 1 mentions same-sex sexual acts, while the theological source emphasizes that one must distinguish the person from the sin; therefore, it is important to speak precisely about the act, rather than reducing the person to it.
concerns_en: The phrase "free from their ruin" speaks too categorically about another person's final destiny; proclaiming the truth does not grant the right to judge individual responsibility or salvation in advance.

A clear emphasis is needed that the condemnation of sin does not mean the rejection or degradation of the person, and that concrete personal guilt cannot be deduced solely from a general moral judgment.

The claim of an organized lobby spreading through various Christian communities is presented without evidence, and the image of a "rainbow flag on the altar" can replace theological reasoning with polemical rhetoric.
The critique of tolerance must distinguish moral approval of actions from respect, dignity, and pastoral closeness toward persons.

sections.subtitle_en: "Blessed are all who fear the Lord" and the danger of tasteless salt
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar testifies: "Brothers and sisters, I fear the Lord"
sections.content_en:
The next part of the interpretation opens with the psalm: **"Blessed is everyone who fears the Lord, who walks in his ways."** The psalm promises that a man will enjoy the fruit of his hands, that his wife will be "like a fruitful vine in the heart of his house", and his sons "like olive shoots around the table". It ends with a blessing from Zion and the desired prosperity of Jerusalem all the days of one's life.

Grebenar immediately offers a personal testimony: **"I fear the Lord."** He is grateful to God for that grace because, as he says, it "keeps him very alert". That is why he does not dare to preach that a man can be saved simply by being good to other people while caring nothing for God.

The host criticizes what he calls **"bland exhortations and homilies"** of the laity and some clerics. He conveys the words of a priest he recently heard at Mass: "If salt loses its taste, it is over; then people trample upon the salt." When a bishop, priest, layman, father of a family, entrepreneur, or political leader does not fear the Lord, Grebenar asserts, everything is all the same to him, so he vividly says that then "even a rainbow flag can be on the altar" and that "the doors are open to everyone".

In contrast to this, he sets Jesus' example: Christ **condemned sin, but freed and healed the sinner**. Many today, according to the host, due to unbelief and a lack of the fear of the Lord, do not condemn sin. Instead, "in the name of tolerance", they accept people who persist in sin without repentance, without even proclaiming Christ to them.

### A Lobby in Christian Churches

Grebenar claims that a certain lobby is growing stronger throughout the Christian world. According to his words, it appeared first among Protestants, then entered the Catholic Church, and "somewhere even among the Orthodox". An increasing number of people among the clergy, he states, say that same-sex relationships are not a sin, while he emphasizes that Sacred Scripture condemns them.

The responsibility of believers here, according to his interpretation, is crucial. Those who defend such a state "in ignorance, in the darkness of the heart" can defend it that way before God. Once they hear the truth and the message from Christians that Jesus has the solution, a free choice lies before them. If they refuse, the believer is "free from their ruin". If, however, believers remain silent about Jesus being the deliverer, the host concludes, "then we are the guilty ones, brothers and sisters, for their ruin".

sections.subtitle: Anegdota s doškolovanja: pitanje o toleranciji koje je izazvalo bijes
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar prepričava iskustvo s predavanja na pedagoškom doškolovanju
sections.content:
Govoreći o pojavi koju vidi kod dijela klera, Grebenar kaže da je riječ o „manjem dijelu, bez dileme, ali ne više ni tako malom“, i da je to sada „čitav pokret“. Takvo stanje, tvrdi, odobravaju i kršteni laici. Kritizira i to što su neke **desne, kršćanske vlade i stranke u Europi i svijetu legalizirale istospolne zajednice** kao bračne zajednice i dale im puna prava, „novcem svih nas, poreznih obveznika“.

Svoju zabrinutost voditelj opisuje slikom **trule jabuke u korpi**, od koje obolijevaju i zdrave. Tvrdi da se upravo to sada događa u društvu i da je sve više mladih učitelja i profesora, po njegovoj ocjeni većinom „indoktriniranih“, koji poučavaju djecu.

### Što se dogodilo na predavanju

Kao potvrdu navodi osobno iskustvo od prije petnaestak godina. Kako bi mogao predavati u srednjoj školi i na fakultetu, morao je položiti osam ispita iz **pedagoških razlika**. Te je ispite tražilo i nekoliko fakulteta u Hrvatskoj, a on je kasnije doista radio na fakultetu kao profesor i predavač. U to je vrijeme, prisjeća se, već imao doktorat, dok su ostali polaznici uglavnom bili studenti četvrte i pete godine, desetak i više godina mlađi od njega.

Predavala im je sveučilišna profesorica, doktorica znanosti s pedagoškog fakulteta, tek nešto starija od njega. Ostalo mu je u sjećanju kako je spomenula da njezina kći, učenica prvog ili drugog razreda srednje škole, idući vikend „treba obaviti krizmu“. Izraz „obaviti krizmu“ posebno mu je zapeo za uho.

Na jednom predavanju profesorica je poručila da budući učitelji moraju djecu i mlade učiti da istospolne odnose treba prihvatiti. Grebenara je šokiralo što se nitko od mlađih kolega nije usprotivio. Njegova bi se generacija, kaže, usprotivila. Zato je sam postavio pitanje: **„Vi kažete da treba biti tolerantan. A tko će biti tolerantan prema nama?“** Mislio je na sebe i mnoge koji to stanje smatraju grijehom.

Reakcija ga je, prema vlastitom opisu, zatekla. Imao je osjećaj „kao da su se vrata pakla otvorila“. Mladi koji su dotad šutjeli počeli su se prema njemu odnositi agresivno i s prezirom. „Ovi da će predavati mojoj djeci u školi? Pa to je pakao“, prisjeća se svoje tadašnje misli.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je djelomično usklađen s katoličkim naukom kada istospolne spolne čine ne poistovjećuje s brakom muškarca i žene te izražava zabrinutost zbog njihova predstavljanja kao moralno prihvatljivih. Ipak, ne razjašnjava ključnu razliku između poštovanja osoba i odobravanja čina, a izrazito alarmistički i generalizirajući prikaz nastavnika može poticati prezir umjesto katolički zahtijevanog poštovanja i suzdržavanja od nepravedne diskriminacije.
concerns: Izraz „istospolne odnose treba prihvatiti” ostaje dvosmislen: može značiti prihvat osoba s dostojanstvom, što Crkva zahtijeva, ili moralno odobravanje istospolnih spolnih čina, koje Crkva ne prihvaća. Bez te razlike slušatelj može pomiješati pastoralno poštovanje s moralnim pristajanjem.

Slika „trule jabuke”, tvrdnja da su mladi učitelji većinom „indoktrinirani” i opis događaja kao otvaranja „vrata pakla” široko pripisuju pokvarenost ili prijetnju skupinama ljudi. Takva retorika može osnažiti neprijateljstvo i nije u skladu s pozivom da se osobe s istospolnim sklonostima prihvaćaju s poštovanjem, suosjećanjem i osjetljivošću te da se izbjegava nepravedna diskriminacija.

Odlomak kritizira javno priznavanje istospolnih zajednica kao braka, što je u skladu s crkvenim razumijevanjem braka, ali prigovor „punim pravima” i javnom novcu iznosi bez razlikovanja pravnog izjednačavanja s brakom od pojedinih pravednih zaštita prava i dostojanstva osoba. Dostavljeni crkveni tekst izričito razlikuje te stvari.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni nauk razlikuje osobu, sklonost i čin: istospolni spolni čini smatra moralno neurednima, ali osobe se moraju prihvaćati s poštovanjem, suosjećanjem i osjetljivošću; Sveto pismo, kako ga tumači Crkva, govori o činima, a ne osuđuje osobu samo zbog sklonosti. Brak se razumije kao zajednica muškarca i žene, utemeljena na spolnoj komplementarnosti i otvorenosti životu, a kršćanski brak ima i sakramentalno značenje. To ne znači da se svako zakonsko postupanje prema istospolnim osobama može svesti na odobravanje spolnih čina: crkveni tekst navodi da se mogu pravno ispravljati pojedine nepravedne situacije na temelju dostojanstva i građanskog statusa, uz očuvanje značenja braka.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is partially aligned with Catholic teaching when it does not equate same-sex sexual acts with the marriage of a man and a woman and expresses concern over their presentation as morally acceptable. However, it does not clarify the key distinction between respect for persons and approval of acts, and the distinctly alarmist and generalizing portrayal of teachers can incite contempt instead of the respect and restraint from unjust discrimination required by Catholicism.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching distinguishes between the person, inclination, and act: it considers same-sex sexual acts to be morally disordered, but persons must be accepted with respect, compassion, and sensitivity; Sacred Scripture, as interpreted by the Church, speaks of acts, and does not condemn the person merely because of inclination. Marriage is understood as a union of a man and a woman, founded upon sexual complementarity and openness to life, and Christian marriage also has a sacramental meaning. This does not mean that every legal treatment of same-sex persons can be reduced to the approval of sexual acts: the ecclesial text states that particular unjust situations can be legally redressed on the basis of dignity and civil status, while preserving the meaning of marriage.
concerns_en: The phrase "same-sex relationships should be accepted" remains ambiguous: it can mean accepting persons with dignity, which the Church requires, or moral approval of same-sex sexual acts, which the Church does not accept. Without that distinction, the listener may confuse pastoral respect with moral assent.

The image of a "rotten apple," the claim that young teachers are mostly "indoctrinated," and the description of the event as the opening of the "gates of hell" broadly attribute corruption or a threat to groups of people. Such rhetoric can strengthen hostility and is not in accordance with the call to accept persons with same-sex inclinations with respect, compassion, and sensitivity, and to avoid unjust discrimination.

The passage criticizes the public recognition of same-sex unions as marriage, which is in line with the Church's understanding of marriage, but raises an objection to "full rights" and public money without distinguishing legal equalization with marriage from particular just protections of the rights and dignity of persons. The provided ecclesial text explicitly distinguishes these things.

sections.subtitle_en: Anecdote from continuing education: a question about tolerance that provoked rage
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar recounts an experience from a lecture during pedagogical continuing education
sections.content_en:
Speaking about the phenomenon he sees among a part of the clergy, Grebenar says that it is a matter of a "smaller part, without dilemma, but no longer so small either," and that this is now an "entire movement." Such a state, he claims, is also approved of by baptized laity. He also criticizes the fact that some **right-wing, Christian governments and parties in Europe and the world have legalized same-sex unions** as marital unions and given them full rights, "with the money of all of us, the taxpayers."

The host describes his concern with the image of a **rotten apple in a basket**, from which healthy ones also become sick. He claims that this is precisely what is happening now in society and that there are more and more young teachers and professors, in his assessment mostly "indoctrinated," who teach children.

### What happened at the lecture

As confirmation, he cites a personal experience from about fifteen years ago. In order to be able to teach in high school and at university, he had to pass eight exams in **pedagogical differences**. Several faculties in Croatia also required these exams, and he later indeed worked at a faculty as a professor and lecturer. At that time, he recalls, he already had a doctorate, while the other participants were mostly fourth- and fifth-year students, about ten or more years younger than him.

They were taught by a university professor, a doctor of science from the pedagogical faculty, only slightly older than him. It remained in his memory how she mentioned that her daughter, a student in the first or second year of high school, the next weekend "needs to do confirmation." The phrase "to do confirmation" particularly caught his ear.

At one lecture, the professor stated that future teachers must teach children and young people that same-sex relationships should be accepted. Grebenar was shocked that none of the younger colleagues objected. His generation, he says, would have objected. Therefore, he himself asked the question: **"You say one should be tolerant. But who will be tolerant towards us?"** He meant himself and the many who consider that state a sin.

The reaction, according to his own description, took him by surprise. He had the feeling "as if the gates of hell had opened." The young people who had been silent until then began to treat him aggressively and with contempt. "These are going to teach my children in school? Why, that is hell," he recalls his thought at the time.

sections.subtitle: Podijeljene zbornice i kako opstati na radnom mjestu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj savjetuje vjernike kako se ponašati na poslu u neprijateljskom okruženju
sections.content:
Iskustvo s predavanja Grebenar povezuje s, kako kaže, „ogromnim problemom u hrvatskom društvu o kojem se ne govori“. Stariji učitelji i profesori često spominju da postoje **podjele u zbornicama**, koje bi se mogle opisati kao podjele na lijevo i desno. To je za njega slika podjele cijelog društva i svijeta.

Voditelj, međutim, poručuje da se zbog toga ne treba brinuti, jer su to **znakovi vremena**. Poziva se na Isusove riječi: **„Nisam došao donijeti mir, nego razdjeljenje.“** Smatra čak da je dobro što se ljudi dijele na Kristove i one koji to nisu, i unutar obitelji i unutar radnih kolektiva. S nekim se mogu dijeliti učionica, prostor i radno vrijeme, ali ne mora se dijeliti slobodno vrijeme. Za takve kolege treba moliti, blagoslivljati ih i navijestiti im Krista ako žele slušati. „Ako neće, ništa, pusti ga“, kaže.

### Sakramentali, molitva i post

Na često pitanje vjernika kako se ponašati na poslu u takvom okruženju, Grebenar odgovara da odgovor daju Sveto pismo i sveti Pavao: od svijeta se ne može pobjeći ni sakriti, ali milost Božja čuva čovjeka. Teret postoji, priznaje, ali postoje i rješenja:

- **sakramentali i medaljice** za zaštitu prostora,
- **molitva** za ljude s kojima se radi,
- **post**, uz savjet: „Posti, pa ćeš vidjeti promjenu.“

Svoj pristup sažima izrekom „klin se klinom izbija“ i dodaje: „Bolje da njega boli glava od utjecaja sakramentala i milosti Božje koja tebe štiti, nego da tebe boli glava od stanja grijeha i posljedica grijeha u kojem se ti ljudi nalaze.“

magisterium.assessment: Navod o Isusu koji donosi „razdjeljenje“ odgovara Lk 12,51, ali se u odlomku ta riječ previše pretvara u opravdanje za aktivno razvrstavanje ljudi i povlačenje iz odnosa, umjesto da se prepozna kako podjela može nastati kao posljedica vjernosti Kristu. Molitva i post za kolege mogu biti dobri, no omalovažavajući ton prema onima koji ne žele slušati i prikaz sakramentala kao zaštitnog sredstva protiv njih ozbiljno zamagljuju kršćansku ljubav i jedinstvo.
concerns: Isusove riječi o razdjeljenju ne znače da kršćani trebaju poticati sukobe ili se radovati podjelama; tumačenje sv. Ivana Zlatoustoga naglašava da rat nije Kristov cilj, nego posljedica ljudskog otpora istini, dok je Kristova volja da ljudi budu sjedinjeni u pobožnosti.

Poziv da se kolege podijele na „Kristove i one koji to nisu“, uz savjet da se onoga tko ne želi slušati jednostavno pusti, može prijeći u osuđivanje i ravnodušnost. Kršćansko svjedočenje treba čuvati istinu, ali i ljubav, strpljivost i nastojanje oko zajedništva; crkveni tekst izričito upozorava na razdor, polemički duh i manjak ljubavi.

Predstavljanje sakramentala i medaljica kao sredstva za zaštitu prostora od kolega ili njihova utjecaja može sugerirati magijsko ili gotovo mehaničko shvaćanje duhovne zaštite. Dostupni izvori ne daju osnovu za tvrdnju da sakramentali djeluju na taj način, niti potvrđuju tvrdnju da će post sam po sebi proizvesti promjenu kod drugih.

Izraz da bi kolegu radije trebala boljeti glava zbog utjecaja sakramentala nego govornika zbog njegova stanja grijeha zvuči neprijateljski i može prikazati druge osobe kao prijetnju, a ne kao bližnje za koje treba moliti i prema kojima treba postupati s ljubavlju.
magisterium.enrichment: Lk 12,51 govori o stvarnom razdjeljenju koje može nastati zbog odgovora na Krista, a ne o općem pozivu na društvenu polarizaciju. Sv. Ivan Zlatousti objašnjava da sukob proizlazi iz ljudskog stava prema istini, a ne iz Kristove namjere da njegovi učenici stvaraju neprijateljstva. Kršćanin može čvrsto svjedočiti vjeru na radnom mjestu, uz molitvu za druge, ali treba paziti da se vjerska razlika ne pretvori u prezir, podjele ili napuštanje dužnosti ljubavi i suradnje.

magisterium.assessment_en: The quote about Jesus bringing "division" corresponds to Lk 12:51, but in the passage this word is turned too much into a justification for actively sorting people and withdrawing from relationships, instead of recognizing how division can arise as a consequence of fidelity to Christ. Prayer and fasting for colleagues can be good, but the disparaging tone toward those who do not want to listen and the portrayal of sacramentals as a means of protection against them seriously obscure Christian love and unity.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Lk 12:51 speaks of real division that can arise because of the response to Christ, not of a general call to social polarization. St. John Chrysostom explains that conflict stems from the human attitude toward the truth, not from Christ's intention that his disciples create enmities. A Christian can firmly witness to the faith in the workplace, with prayer for others, but must take care that religious difference does not turn into contempt, divisions, or the abandonment of the duty of love and cooperation.
concerns_en: Jesus' words about division do not mean that Christians should incite conflicts or rejoice in divisions; the interpretation of St. John Chrysostom emphasizes that war is not Christ's goal, but the consequence of human resistance to the truth, while Christ's will is that people be united in godliness.

The call to divide colleagues into "those of Christ and those who are not", along with the advice to simply let go of whoever does not want to listen, can turn into condemnation and indifference. Christian witness must preserve truth, but also love, patience, and effort toward communion; Church text explicitly warns against discord, a polemical spirit, and a lack of love.

Presenting sacramentals and medals as a means of protecting space from colleagues or their influence can suggest a magical or almost mechanical understanding of spiritual protection. Available sources provide no basis for the claim that sacramentals work in that way, nor do they confirm the claim that fasting will in itself produce change in others.

The expression that a colleague's head should rather ache from the influence of sacramentals than the speaker's from their state of sin sounds hostile and can portray other people as a threat, rather than as neighbors for whom one should pray and toward whom one should act with love.

sections.subtitle_en: Divided staff rooms and how to survive in the workplace
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host advises believers on how to behave at work in a hostile environment
sections.content_en:
Grebenar connects the experience from the lecture with, as he says, a "huge problem in Croatian society that is not spoken about". Older teachers and professors often mention that there are **divisions in staff rooms**, which could be described as divisions into left and right. For him, this is an image of the division of the whole society and the world.

The host, however, conveys that one should not worry because of this, because these are **signs of the times**. He refers to Jesus' words: **"I have not come to bring peace, but division."** He even considers it good that people are divided into those of Christ and those who are not, both within the family and within work collectives. With someone, one can share a classroom, space, and working hours, but one does not have to share free time. One should pray for such colleagues, bless them, and proclaim Christ to them if they want to listen. "If he won't, nothing, let him be," he says.

### Sacramentals, prayer, and fasting

To the frequent question of believers about how to behave at work in such an environment, Grebenar answers that Sacred Scripture and Saint Paul give the answer: one cannot escape or hide from the world, but the grace of God preserves a person. A burden exists, he admits, but solutions also exist:

- **sacramentals and medals** for the protection of space,
- **prayer** for the people with whom one works,
- **fasting**, with the advice: "Fast, and you will see change."

He summarizes his approach with the saying "one wedge drives out another" and adds: "It is better that his head aches from the influence of sacramentals and the grace of God that protects you, than that your head aches from the state of sin and the consequences of sin in which those people find themselves."

sections.subtitle: Strah Božji nije strah od kazne: čiji sud zaista ima težinu
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar objašnjava da se ne boji Božje kazne, nego toga da iznevjeri savez
sections.content:
Vraćajući se psalmu, Grebenar svjedoči da je njegov život blagoslovljen, kao i njegova obitelj, i da je sretan što to može reći. U istom dahu naglašava da se **„jako boji Gospodina“**. Odmah pojašnjava da to nije strah da će ga Bog kazniti. Takvu sliku Boga, tvrdi, nameće đavao jer je sam takav, a „Bog ne želi kažnjavati i ne kažnjava“.

Na pitanje čega se onda boji, voditelj odgovara: boji se da **nije dobra „druga strana“ u savezu između sebe i Boga**. Taj strah objašnjava usporedbom iz obiteljskog života. Jako bi ga pogodilo kad bi mu djeca rekla: „Ti nisi bio dobar tata za nas.“ Jednako bi ga pogodilo kad bi mu supruga rekla da kao muž nije ispunio svoju misiju i zadaću. To bi mu bilo teško upravo zato što su oni „u vjeri i vole Isusa“.

### Kad prijekor postaje „melem za uši“

Sasvim je drukčije, tumači Grebenar, kada isto kaže netko tko nije u vjeri, primjerice rodbina ili krvni srodnici koji žive u smrtnom grijehu i ne obraćaju se unatoč svjedočanstvu. Ako mu takav netko kaže „Ti si me razočarao, nisi čovjek“, on se toga ne boji. Takve bi riječi doživio kao **„melem za uši“** i znak da se ostvaruje Evanđelje. Poziva se na Isusove riječi: **„Tko više ljubi oca ili majku nego mene, nije mene dostojan.“**

Prava težina leži u sudu onoga tko je Božji: brata u Gospodinu koji ljubi Isusa i koji je za Isusa donio neke plodove. Kad bi mu takav rekao „Ti nisi izvršio volju Gospodnju“, toga bi se, priznaje, bojao. „Uvijek je pitanje tko govori“, zaključuje voditelj.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na sinovskom strahu — bojazni da se ne izgubi pravednost i ne iznevjeri odnos s Bogom — te na prvenstvu ljubavi prema Kristu uglavnom je u skladu s kršćanskom vjerom. Ipak, tvrdnja da Bog „ne želi kažnjavati i ne kažnjava” nije usklađena s biblijskim govorom o Božjem sudu, a opis prijekora nevjernih rođaka kao „melema za uši” može navesti na odbacivanje istinite opomene zbog toga tko je izgovara.
concerns: Katolička tradicija razlikuje servilni strah od kazne i sinovski strah da se ne uvrijedi Boga ili izgubi pravednost, ali ne proglašava svaki strah od kazne pogrešnim: taj strah može biti dobar i pripraviti čovjeka na ljubav. Izjava da Bog ne kažnjava zanemaruje biblijsko i kršćansko učenje o Božjoj pravednosti i sudu.

Isusove riječi o ljubavi prema njemu više nego prema ocu ili majci potvrđuju da vjernost Kristu ima prvenstvo, ali same po sebi ne opravdavaju prezir prema članovima obitelji niti zaključak da je njihov prijekor znak da se ostvaruje Evanđelje.

Procjena opomene samo prema tome je li govornik „u vjeri” može podcijeniti istinitu kritiku osobe izvan Crkve ili precijeniti kritiku vjernika: važni su istinitost sadržaja i plodovi savjeta, ne samo identitet govornika.
magisterium.enrichment: Sveti Augustin razlikuje strah od kazne od čistoga straha koji se boji izgubiti pravednost; ljubav ne uklanja taj drugi strah, nego ga učvršćuje. Isusova zapovijed da ga ljubimo više od najbližih traži da obiteljske veze ne stavimo iznad Boga, a ne da ih preziremo. Zato se Božje milosrđe ne bi smjelo prikazivati kao odsutnost suda: kršćanska predaja može zajedno govoriti o Božjoj dobroti, pozivu na obraćenje i pravednom sudu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on filial fear — the apprehension of losing righteousness and failing the relationship with God — as well as on the primacy of love for Christ is generally in accordance with the Christian faith. However, the claim that God "does not want to punish and does not punish" is not aligned with biblical discourse on God's judgment, and describing the reproach of unbelieving relatives as "music to one's ears" can lead to rejecting a truthful admonition because of who utters it.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Saint Augustine distinguishes the fear of punishment from the chaste fear that dreads losing righteousness; love does not eliminate this second fear, but rather strengthens it. Jesus' commandment to love him more than our closest relatives requires that we do not place family ties above God, not that we despise them. Therefore, God's mercy should not be presented as the absence of judgment: Christian tradition can speak together of God's goodness, the call to conversion, and righteous judgment.
concerns_en: Catholic tradition distinguishes servile fear of punishment from filial fear of offending God or losing righteousness, but it does not declare every fear of punishment to be wrong: that fear can be good and prepare a person for love. The statement that God does not punish disregards biblical and Christian teaching on God's justice and judgment.

Jesus' words about loving him more than father or mother confirm that fidelity to Christ has primacy, but in themselves they do not justify contempt toward family members or the conclusion that their reproach is a sign that the Gospel is being fulfilled.

Evaluating an admonition solely according to whether the speaker is "in the faith" can underestimate truthful criticism from a person outside the Church or overestimate criticism from a believer: the truthfulness of the content and the fruits of the counsel are important, not just the identity of the speaker.

sections.subtitle_en: Fear of God is not fear of punishment: whose judgment truly has weight
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar explains that he does not fear God's punishment, but rather failing the covenant
sections.content_en:
Returning to the psalm, Grebenar testifies that his life is blessed, as is his family, and that he is happy to be able to say so. In the same breath, he emphasizes that he **"fears the Lord greatly"**. He immediately clarifies that this is not a fear that God will punish him. Such an image of God, he claims, is imposed by the devil because he himself is like that, while "God does not want to punish and does not punish."

To the question of what he is afraid of then, the host replies: he fears **not being a good "other party" in the covenant between himself and God**. He explains this fear through a comparison from family life. It would hit him hard if his children told him: "You were not a good dad to us." It would hit him equally hard if his wife told him that as a husband he did not fulfill his mission and task. That would be difficult for him precisely because they are "in the faith and love Jesus."

### When reproach becomes "music to one's ears"

It is completely different, Grebenar explains, when the same is said by someone who is not in the faith, for example relatives or blood relations who live in mortal sin and do not convert despite the witness. If someone like that tells him "You disappointed me, you are not a human being," he is not afraid of that. He would experience such words as **"music to one's ears"** and a sign that the Gospel is being fulfilled. He refers to Jesus' words: **"Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me."**

The real weight lies in the judgment of one who belongs to God: a brother in the Lord who loves Jesus and who has borne some fruits for Jesus. If someone like that told him "You did not carry out the will of the Lord," he admits he would fear that. "It is always a question of who is speaking," the host concludes.

sections.subtitle: Kad se djeca okrenu od vjere: slobodna volja i biblijski primjeri
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj navodi primjer sinova proroka Samuela i svećenika Elija
sections.content:
Iz pitanja „tko govori“ Grebenar prelazi na bolnu temu mnogih roditelja: djecu koja su se, unatoč primljenoj vjeri, „odmetnula i otišla u grijeh“. Podsjeća da dijete ima **slobodnu volju** i može ići kamo želi. „Nismo mi gospodari svoje djece“, kaže. Roditelji ostaju roditelji cijeli život, ali dolazi trenutak kada se sin ili kći osamostaljuju i sami biraju put, bez obzira na vjeru koju su im roditelji prenijeli.

Roditelj je, naglašava voditelj, mogao biti izvrstan i svjedočiti vjeru, a dijete se ipak moglo okrenuti protiv. Takvih primjera ima i u Svetom pismu. **Sinovi proroka Samuela** nisu išli stopama svoga oca, a slično je bilo i sa **sinovima svećenika Elija**. „Kako je to moguće? Ovaj je bio tako velik prorok Samuel, a djeca nisu išla stopama svoga oca. Moguće je. Bog daje slobodan izbor svima“, objašnjava.

Zato roditeljima koji od takve djece čuju „Ti nisi dobar otac“ ili „Ne valjaš“ Grebenar poručuje da im to, „nažalost“, treba biti na radost, jer drukčije ni ne mogu čuti ako su Božji. Neka ih to utješi, kaže, jer mnogi roditelji trpe isto.

Voditelj nabraja i druge prizore koje roditelji proživljavaju: djecu koja čekaju da roditelji umru kako bi podijelila imovinu, djecu bez potomstva te braću i sestre koji međusobno ne razgovaraju. Roditelji se tada pitaju: „Zar su ovo moja djeca?“ Svijet, zaključuje, može utjecati tako da odvoji djecu, pa je zato uvijek važno imati Isusa na prvom mjestu i bojati se Boga tako da ga se ne povrijedi.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: ispravno priznaje slobodu djece i navodi biblijske primjere Samuelovih i Elijevih sinova, koji nisu slijedili put svojih očeva. Ipak, tvrdnja da roditelje treba radovati kada im djeca kažu da nisu dobri roditelji može pogrešno poistovjetiti bolnu kritiku s dokazom vjernosti Bogu te zanemariti mogućnost da roditelj ipak treba ispitati vlastito ponašanje.
concerns: Poruka da su uvrede ili osude djece „na radost” roditeljima, „jer drukčije ni ne mogu čuti ako su Božji”, previše je općenita: protivljenje roditelju samo po sebi ne dokazuje njegovu svetost niti znači da je svaka kritika nepravedna.

Naglasak na slobodnoj volji ne bi smio ostaviti dojam da roditelji nemaju dužnost odgajati djecu u vjeri ili da su oslobođeni samopropitivanja; Katolička crkva potvrđuje i roditeljsko pravo i dužnost kršćanskog odgoja.
magisterium.enrichment: Prva Samuelova knjiga potvrđuje da Samuelovi sinovi nisu išli njegovim putom, nego su primali mito i izvrćali pravdu; o Elijevim se sinovima govori kao o onima koji su prezirali Gospodinove prinose, a Eli ih je zbog zla ukorio, no nisu poslušali očev glas. Kongregacija za nauk vjere uči da roditelji ne trebaju sebi predbacivati što su krstili dijete i odgajali ga kršćanski ako ono poslije odbaci svoje obveze, ali ih poziva da i dalje svjedoče vjeru strpljivošću, ljubavlju i molitvom. Stoga slobodu djece treba držati zajedno s trajnom roditeljskom odgovornošću i nadom, a strah Božji razumjeti kao poštovanje Boga koje vodi vjernosti, ne kao razlog da se svaka obiteljska osuda prihvati kao potvrda vlastite pravednosti.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: it correctly recognizes the freedom of children and cites biblical examples of the sons of Samuel and Eli, who did not follow the path of their fathers. Nevertheless, the claim that parents should rejoice when their children tell them they are not good parents may mistakenly equate painful criticism with proof of fidelity to God and overlook the possibility that the parent still needs to examine their own behavior.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The First Book of Samuel confirms that Samuel's sons did not walk in his ways, but took bribes and perverted justice; Eli's sons are spoken of as those who despised the Lord's offerings, and Eli rebuked them because of their evil, but they did not listen to their father's voice. The Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith teaches that parents should not reproach themselves for having baptized a child and brought it up Christianly if it later rejects its obligations, but calls them to continue witnessing to the faith through patience, love, and prayer. Therefore, the freedom of children should be held together with enduring parental responsibility and hope, and the fear of God understood as reverence for God that leads to fidelity, not as a reason to accept every family condemnation as confirmation of one's own righteousness.
concerns_en: The message that insults or condemnations from children are "for joy" to parents, "because they cannot even hear otherwise if they belong to God", is too general: opposition to a parent in itself does not prove their holiness, nor does it mean that every criticism is unjust.

The emphasis on free will should not leave the impression that parents have no duty to raise children in the faith or that they are exempt from self-examination; the Catholic Church affirms both the parental right and duty of Christian upbringing.

sections.subtitle_en: When children turn away from faith: free will and biblical examples
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host cites the example of the sons of the prophet Samuel and the priest Eli
sections.content_en:
From the question "who is speaking", Grebenar moves to the painful topic of many parents: children who, despite the faith they received, have "rebelled and gone into sin". He reminds that a child has **free will** and can go where it wants. "We are not the masters of our children," he says. Parents remain parents their whole life, but the moment comes when a son or daughter becomes independent and chooses their path on their own, regardless of the faith their parents passed on to them.

A parent, the host emphasizes, could have been excellent and witnessed to the faith, and yet the child could have turned against it. There are such examples in Sacred Scripture as well. The **sons of the prophet Samuel** did not follow in the footsteps of their father, and it was similar with the **sons of the priest Eli**. "How is that possible? This Samuel was such a great prophet, and the children did not follow in the footsteps of their father. It is possible. God gives free choice to everyone," he explains.

Therefore, to parents who hear from such children "You are not a good father" or "You are no good", Grebenar says that, "unfortunately", this should be for joy to them, because they cannot even hear otherwise if they belong to God. Let that comfort them, he says, because many parents suffer the same.

The host also lists other scenes that parents experience: children who wait for their parents to die in order to divide the property, children without offspring, and brothers and sisters who do not speak to each other. Parents then ask themselves: "Are these my children?" The world, he concludes, can exert influence so as to separate children, which is why it is always important to have Jesus in first place and to fear God so as not to hurt Him.

sections.subtitle: „Odlazite od mene, bezakonici“: opomena onima koji samo slave
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar citira Isusove riječi karizmaticima koji su prorokovali i izgonili zle duhove
sections.content:
Najdublji izvor svoga straha Grebenar opisuje kao bojazan da mu Gospodin jednog dana ne kaže: **„Odlazi od mene, bezakoniče.“** Podsjeća na evanđeoski prizor u kojem se ljudi pozivaju na svoje karizme: „Gospodine, Gospodine, zar nismo mi u tvoje ime prorokovali, u tvoje ime čudesa činili, u tvoje ime liječili, zle duhove izgonili?“ Isus im ipak odgovara: „Odlazite od mene, bezakonici.“

Voditelj prepričava kako ga je o tom odlomku upitao „jedan dobar svećenik“: „Brate, kako je to moguće? Što ti misliš o tome?“ Grebenar mu je savjetovao da pročita prethodni dio teksta, u kojem Isus govori o **prokazivanju zla i o tami koja mora biti raskrinkana i iznesena na svjetlo**. Odgovor po njegovu mišljenju leži upravo u tome: ti karizmatici su prešutjeli i **nisu se suprotstavili zlu**. Ostalo je samo „dizanje ruku i slavljenje i ništa više“.

Vršenje volje Božje, tumači Grebenar, obvezuje vjernika da prokazuje zlo i raskrinkava tamu kako bi bila svjetlost. Uz to dodaje ključno ograničenje: **ne raskrinkavati ljude, nego grijeh**. Vjeruje da je to barem djelomično učinio i u ovoj emisiji, govoreći o pastirima, političarima, poduzetnicima i običnim vjernicima koji idu na misu, pričešćuju se i ispovijedaju, a istodobno odobravaju ono što on smatra grijehom.

### „Što me briga što rade u četiri zida“

Voditelj se osvrće na čest stav da se nitko ne treba miješati u to što dvojica muškaraca rade „u četiri zida“. To je, priznaje, djelomično točno: što netko radi u svoja četiri zida, njegov je izbor. Situacija se za njega mijenja kada isti ljudi kažu da žele djecu i da žele **posvojiti djecu koju su roditelji napustili**. Tada se, kaže, kao otac osjeća obveznim reagirati. Tvrdi da bi se tako „na djeci liječile vlastite traume“, uz obrazloženje da „nema nitko tko je izabrao grijeh, a da nije istraumatiziran grijehom“.

magisterium.assessment: Upozorenje da karizme i religiozne geste ne zamjenjuju vršenje Očeve volje vjerno odražava Mt 7,21–23, a poziv da se osuđuje grijeh, ne ponižava osobe, može biti u skladu s kršćanskim svjedočenjem. Ipak, tumačenje da je razlog Isusove osude baš to što se ljudi nisu suprotstavili zlu nije izričito naveden u odlomku, dok su tvrdnje o traumi i posvajanju iznesene preširoko i bez dostatnog teološkog ili biblijskog temelja.
concerns: Mt 7,21–23 povezuje odbacivanje s nevršenjem Očeve volje i bezakonjem, ali ne kaže da su ti ljudi osuđeni upravo zato što nisu raskrinkavali zlo; to je moguće primjensko tumačenje, a ne izravan smisao citata.

Tvrdnja da nema osobe koja je izabrala grijeh a da nije istraumatizirana grijehom univerzalna je psihološka tvrdnja koju raspoloživi izvori ne potvrđuju; potrebno je razlikovati moralnu prosudbu čina od prosudbe osobne krivnje i okolnosti.

Crkveni izvor traži da se istodobno izbjegavaju odobravanje homoseksualnih čina i nepravedna diskriminacija osoba, te potiče razborito i diskretno svjedočenje; taj pastoralni obzir treba biti jasno vidljiv uz osudu grijeha.

Crkveni dokument iznosi prigovor zakonskom izjednačavanju istospolnih zajednica s brakom i njihovu pristupu posvajanju, ali odlomak ne opravdava tvrdnju da bi se posvojenjem nužno liječile traume posvojitelja ili da se može unaprijed suditi o motivima konkretnih osoba.
magisterium.enrichment: U Mt 7 Isus ne odbacuje karizme kao takve, nego upozorava da izvanjski religiozni uspjesi ne mogu zamijeniti poslušnost Bogu i život u skladu s njegovom voljom. Katoličko svjedočenje o moralnom zlu treba zato spajati istinu s poštovanjem, suosjećanjem i odbacivanjem nepravedne diskriminacije. Kad se govori o posvajanju, valja razlikovati crkveni moralni sud o naravi braka i obiteljskog okruženja od neutemeljenih pretpostavki o psihičkom stanju ili namjerama pojedinih ljudi.

magisterium.assessment_en: The warning that charisms and religious gestures do not replace doing the Father's will faithfully reflects Mt 7:21–23, and the call to condemn sin without humiliating persons can be in accordance with Christian witness. However, the interpretation that the reason for Jesus' condemnation is precisely that people did not oppose evil is not explicitly stated in the passage, while the claims regarding trauma and adoption are presented too broadly and without sufficient theological or biblical foundation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Mt 7, Jesus does not reject charisms as such, but warns that external religious successes cannot replace obedience to God and a life in accordance with His will. Catholic witness regarding moral evil should therefore combine truth with respect, compassion, and the rejection of unjust discrimination. When speaking about adoption, one must distinguish the Church's moral judgment on the nature of marriage and the family environment from unfounded assumptions about the psychological state or intentions of individual people.
concerns_en: Mt 7:21–23 links rejection with not doing the Father's will and with lawlessness, but it does not state that these people are condemned precisely because they did not unmask evil; this is a possible applied interpretation, not the direct meaning of the quotation.

The claim that there is no person who has chosen sin without being traumatized by sin is a universal psychological claim that available sources do not confirm; it is necessary to distinguish the moral judgment of an act from the judgment of personal culpability and circumstances.

The Church source requires that both approval of homosexual acts and unjust discrimination against persons be avoided at the same time, and encourages prudent and discreet witness; this pastoral consideration should be clearly evident alongside the condemnation of sin.

The Church document raises an objection to the legal equation of same-sex unions with marriage and their access to adoption, but the passage does not justify the claim that adoption would necessarily treat the adopters' traumas or that one can judge in advance the motives of specific persons.

sections.subtitle_en: “Depart from me, evildoers”: a warning to those who only praise
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar quotes Jesus' words to charismatics who prophesied and cast out evil spirits
sections.content_en:
The deepest source of his fear Grebenar describes as the dread that the Lord might one day say to him: **“Depart from me, evildoer.”** He recalls the Gospel scene in which people appeal to their charisms: “Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, perform miracles in your name, heal in your name, cast out evil spirits?” Jesus nevertheless answers them: “Depart from me, evildoers.”

The host recounts how “a good priest” asked him about that passage: “Brother, how is that possible? What do you think about it?” Grebenar advised him to read the preceding part of the text, in which Jesus speaks about **denouncing evil and about the darkness that must be unmasked and brought into the light**. The answer, in his opinion, lies precisely in that: those charismatics remained silent and **did not oppose evil**. All that remained was “raising hands and praising, and nothing more”.

Doing the will of God, Grebenar explains, obligates the believer to denounce evil and unmask darkness so that there may be light. To this he adds a key limitation: **not unmasking people, but sin**. He believes that he did this at least partially in this episode as well, speaking about pastors, politicians, entrepreneurs, and ordinary believers who go to Mass, receive Communion, and go to confession, while at the same time approving what he considers sin.

### “What do I care what they do within four walls”

The host reflects on the common attitude that no one should interfere in what two men do “within four walls.” That is, he admits, partially true: what someone does within their four walls is their choice. The situation changes for him when the same people say that they want children and that they want to **adopt children abandoned by their parents**. Then, he says, as a father he feels obliged to react. He claims that in this way “one's own traumas would be treated on children,” with the reasoning that “there is no one who has chosen sin without being traumatized by sin.”

sections.subtitle: Što je grijeh uči Sveto pismo, a ne zakonodavci
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj kritizira parolu „Isus voli sve ljude“ i naglašava da Isus mrzi grijeh
sections.content:
Na pitanje što jest, a što nije grijeh, Grebenar odgovara kratko: **„To uči Sveto pismo i točka.“** Ne određuje to predsjednik države, premijer ni zakonodavci, „ovi što dižu ruku za **Istanbulsku konvenciju** pa idu u crkvu“. Sveto pismo uči, a biskupi i kler ga tumače. Ako tumače dobro, poučavaju narod. Ako ne tumače dobro, upozorava voditelj, mogu narod „strovaliti u pakao, bar tamo gdje djeluju“.

Zato mu je sablažnjivo gledati, kako kaže, zalaganje „ne baš malog broja ljudi“ u Crkvi, pa i u Katoličkoj Crkvi, koji bi trebali raskrinkati i prokazati zlo, a umjesto toga ponavljaju parolu **„Isus voli sve ljude“**. Takvu izjavu u ovom kontekstu naziva licemjernom i izdajničkom. Naravno da Isus voli sve ljude i da je za sve umro na križu, kaže, ali **Isus mrzi grijeh**. Ljudi koji vole grijeh na način da ga se ne žele odreći, tvrdi Grebenar, „zapravo mrze Isusa“.

Kao vrhunac takve logike navodi ideju da bi Crkva, „koja se piše velikim slovom“, mogla otvoriti vrata „sodomskoj katoličkoj molitvenoj zajednici“ osoba u istospolnim zajednicama. To ocjenjuje kao „van svake pameti“.

### Pogled prema Francuskoj i školama

Posljedice, po njegovu mišljenju, već su vidljive u **Francuskoj**, gdje upire prstom u mlade od 15, 16 i 17 godina: „Vidi što si odgojio.“ Podsjeća na svoje iskustvo s predavanja od prije desetak do petnaest godina i dodaje da su takvi, koji su „skočili na njega“, danas učitelji koji odgajaju djecu. U **Hercegovini**, „Bogu hvala“, to nije slučaj, ali „ima toga po Hrvatskoj“.

Prenosi i pritužbe prosvjetnih radnika koji su članovi domoljubne inicijative Ora et labora. Oni se žale da preko političkih veza, primjerice kao rođaci nekog načelnika ili „lokalnog šerifa“, u škole dolaze mladi tek svršeni studenti bez djece, „probušenih noseva, ušiju i jezika“. Voditelj se pita kako takvi mogu odgajati djecu kada ni sami, po njegovim riječima, nisu stekli odgoj.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak ispravno ističe da kršćansko moralno prosuđivanje ne određuju političari te da se, prema katoličkom nauku, homoseksualni čini ne mogu moralno odobriti. Ipak, način na koji iznosi taj nauk mjestimice je preoštar i nedovoljno razlučuje moralnu prosudbu čina od poštovanja osobe, osobne krivnje i pastorala.
concerns: Tvrdnja da oni koji ne žele napustiti grijeh „zapravo mrze Isusa“ preširoko pripisuje unutarnji stav i osobnu krivnju. Katolički nauk razlikuje objektivnu moralnu prosudbu čina od stupnja osobne odgovornosti; osobe s homoseksualnim sklonostima treba prihvaćati s poštovanjem, suosjećanjem i osjetljivošću, bez nepravedne diskriminacije.

Rečenica „Sveto pismo i točka“ može ostaviti dojam da tumačenje Svetoga pisma nije potrebno. Sam odlomak priznaje da ga biskupi i kler tumače, a katolička procjena moralnih pitanja traži pažljivo čitanje biblijskih tekstova u njihovu kontekstu i vjernost crkvenom nauku; biblijska komisija, primjerice, upozorava da biblijski tekstovi o homoseksualnim činima nisu svi istoga književnog roda ni jednake važnosti.

Sama činjenica da bi molitvena zajednica primala osobe u istospolnim zajednicama ne dokazuje da Crkva odobrava njihove čine. Crkveni nauk ne odobrava homoseksualne čine, ali također nalaže poštovanje osoba; potrebno je razlikovati pastoralnu dobrodošlicu i molitvu od moralnog odobravanja veze ili čina.

Izgled učitelja, poput piercinga, sam po sebi ne dokazuje da osoba nije odgojena ili nesposobna odgajati djecu. Odlomak za takav zaključak ne nudi teološki ni drugi dokaz, pa taj dio riskira nepravedno omalovažavanje ljudi na temelju izgleda.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička prosudba drži zajedno dvije stvari: homoseksualne čini ne mogu biti moralno odobreni, a osobe s homoseksualnim sklonostima moraju biti prihvaćene s poštovanjem i bez nepravedne diskriminacije. Isusov poziv na obraćenje ne svodi se na osudu: kršćanska poruka govori i o mogućnosti povratka i o Božjem milosrđu, pa istina o grijehu treba biti naviještena bez proglašavanja da pojedina osoba mrzi Boga ili da joj je poznata osobna krivnja.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage correctly emphasizes that Christian moral judgment is not determined by politicians and that, according to Catholic teaching, homosexual acts cannot be morally approved. However, the way in which it presents this teaching is in places too harsh and insufficiently distinguishes the moral judgment of the act from respect for the person, personal guilt, and pastoral care.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic judgment holds two things together: homosexual acts cannot be morally approved, and persons with homosexual tendencies must be accepted with respect and without unjust discrimination. Jesus' call to conversion does not reduce to condemnation: the Christian message also speaks of the possibility of return and of God's mercy, so the truth about sin should be proclaimed without declaring that an individual person hates God or that their personal guilt is known.
concerns_en: The claim that those who do not want to abandon sin "actually hate Jesus" too broadly attributes an internal attitude and personal guilt. Catholic teaching distinguishes the objective moral judgment of an act from the degree of personal responsibility; persons with homosexual tendencies should be accepted with respect, compassion, and sensitivity, without unjust discrimination.

The sentence "Sacred Scripture and period" can give the impression that the interpretation of Sacred Scripture is not necessary. The passage itself acknowledges that the bishops and clergy interpret it, and Catholic assessment of moral questions requires careful reading of biblical texts in their context and fidelity to Church teaching; the biblical commission, for example, warns that biblical texts about homosexual acts are not all of the same literary genre nor of equal importance.

The mere fact that a prayer community would receive persons in same-sex unions does not prove that the Church approves their acts. Church teaching does not approve homosexual acts, but also mandates respect for persons; it is necessary to distinguish pastoral welcome and prayer from moral approval of a union or act.

The appearance of teachers, such as piercings, does not in itself prove that a person is not well-raised or is incapable of raising children. The passage offers neither theological nor other proof for such a conclusion, so that part risks unjustly disparaging people on the basis of appearance.

sections.subtitle_en: What is sin is taught by Sacred Scripture, not lawmakers
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host criticizes the slogan "Jesus loves all people" and emphasizes that Jesus hates sin
sections.content_en:
To the question of what is and what is not sin, Grebenar answers briefly: **"Sacred Scripture teaches that, and period."** It is not determined by the president of the state, the prime minister, nor lawmakers, "those who raise their hands for the **Istanbul Convention** and then go to church." Sacred Scripture teaches, and bishops and clergy interpret it. If they interpret well, they instruct the people. If they do not interpret well, the host warns, they can "hurl the people into hell, at least where they operate."

Therefore, it is scandalous for him to watch, as he says, the advocacy of "not a small number of people" in the Church, and even in the Catholic Church, who should unmask and denounce evil, but instead repeat the slogan **"Jesus loves all people"**. He calls such a statement in this context hypocritical and treacherous. Of course Jesus loves all people and died on the cross for everyone, he says, but **Jesus hates sin**. People who love sin in such a way that they do not want to renounce it, Grebenar claims, "actually hate Jesus."

As the culmination of such logic, he cites the idea that the Church, "which is capitalized," could open its doors to a "sodomite Catholic prayer community" of persons in same-sex unions. He evaluates this as "beyond all reason."

### A look toward France and schools

The consequences, in his opinion, are already visible in **France**, where he points his finger at young people aged 15, 16, and 17: "Look what you raised." He recalls his experience from lectures ten to fifteen years ago and adds that such people, who "jumped on him," are today teachers who raise children. In **Hercegovina**, "thank God," that is not the case, but "there is that across Croatia."

He also conveys the complaints of educators who are members of the patriotic initiative Ora et labora. They complain that through political connections, for example as relatives of some mayor or "local sheriff," young, freshly graduated students without children, "with pierced noses, ears, and tongues," come into schools. The host wonders how such people can raise children when they themselves, in his words, have not acquired an upbringing.

sections.subtitle: Slavljenje bez suprotstavljanja zlu i osobna odgovornost javnih osoba
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar govori o osobnoj odgovornosti da talente iskoristi za javno suprotstavljanje zlu
sections.content:
Završnu cjelinu ove iteracije Grebenar posvećuje pobožnosti koja ne prelazi u djelovanje. Ako vjernici dižu ruke, slave Isusa i organiziraju duhovne obnove na kojima je „sve lijepo“, a istodobno šute o zlu koje je postalo javno i ne usuđuju se javno mu se suprotstaviti, tada, kaže, **„odgovaramo definiciji bezakonika“**. Šuti se na bezakonje, a „ovamo kao slavimo Isusa“, makar to bila i molitva krunice na trgu ili djelovanje u molitvenim zajednicama.

Tu odgovornost primjenjuje i na sebe. Navodi da vodi molitvenu zajednicu za koju kaže da je trenutno **najveća molitvena zajednica na svijetu koja svaki dan moli i posti**. Opisuje je kao plod autentične **međugorske duhovnosti** u kojoj ljudi uče moliti krunicu i razmatrati Sveto pismo, „pa makar neki škrgutali zubima na to“.

To što ga toliki ljudi slušaju pripisuje milosti Božjoj, a ne vlastitoj pameti, jer mu je Gospodin dao da može tumačiti Sveto pismo. Ističe, međutim, da postoji dio koji ovisi isključivo o njemu. „Osobno ja, Vladimir Grebenar“, kaže, slobodnom voljom biram hoću li talente koje mi je Bog dao koristiti da raskrinkam zlo i suprotstavim mu se. Spreman je, poručuje, da ga udare „bičevi koji su udarali Isusa“, kad već moli „daj mi dio svoje muke i patnje“. Tko tako moli, dodaje, neka ne bude licemjer, nego neka se zlu suprotstavi javno.

### Poziv političarima, poduzetnicima i kleru

Poruku izričito upućuje svima koji djeluju u javnosti:

- **političarima**,
- **poduzetnicima**,
- **voditeljima molitvenih zajednica**,
- **javnim osobama iz klera**.

Od njih se, kaže, očekuje da se **javno konfrontiraju zlu**. Oštro kritizira one koji umjesto toga napadaju upravo one koji to čine, dok sami ostaju „lijepo u četiri zida, gdje je dobar obrok“. Takvi se zatim, prema njegovu opisu, pojavljuju na televiziji i društvenim mrežama „da se njih vidi“, jer im je „došlo pet minuta slave“.

magisterium.assessment: Središnja poruka — da molitva i slavljenje ne smiju postati izgovor za ravnodušnost prema grijehu, nepravdi i ranjivima — uglavnom je usklađena s katoličkim naukom: kršćanin je pozvan biti javni svjedok i djelovati za dobro. Ipak, tvrdnju da šutnja znači da netko „odgovara definiciji bezakonika” treba ublažiti: javno suprotstavljanje zlu nije uvijek jedini mudar ili moralno obvezan oblik svjedočenja, a osuda tuđih motiva zahtijeva oprez.
concerns: Izraz „odgovaramo definiciji bezakonika” može nepravedno generalizirati različite slučajeve šutnje: razboritost, zaštita drugih ili nedostatak pouzdanih informacija mogu utjecati na to kako i kada netko treba govoriti. Crkveno učenje potiče na obranu slabih i traženje pravde, ali priznaje i nenametljive oblike svjedočenja te podnošenje nepravde iz ljubavi prema Bogu.

Poziv na javno suprotstavljanje zlu treba uključivati istinoljubivost, razboritost i blagost; kritika koja drugima pripisuje taštinu ili želju za slavom bez dovoljno osnove može prijeći u nepošteno osuđivanje.

Govor o primanju Isusove muke može se razumjeti katolički kao spremnost podnositi teškoće u sjedinjenju s Kristom, ali ne kao poistovjećivanje vlastite patnje s jedinstvenom Kristovom otkupiteljskom žrtvom.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveno učenje ne suprotstavlja molitvu i društvenu odgovornost: isti Krist kojem se vjernik klanja prisutan je i u ljudima kojima je potrebna pomoć, a vjera treba oblikovati djelovanje u javnom životu. Svjedočenje može uključivati hrabro neslaganje, zahtijevanje pravde i obranu slabih, ali i strpljivost, blagost ili podnošenje nepravde kada to okolnosti razborito traže. Zato je najtočniji naglasak odlomka da molitva treba voditi vjernika prema odgovornoj ljubavi, a ne da svaki oblik šutnje automatski dokazuje nevjernost.

magisterium.assessment_en: The central message—that prayer and praise must not become an excuse for indifference toward sin, injustice, and the vulnerable—is generally aligned with Catholic teaching: the Christian is called to be a public witness and to act for the good. Nevertheless, the claim that silence means someone “fits the definition of the lawless” needs to be qualified: publicly opposing evil is not always the only wise or morally obligatory form of witness, and judging others' motives requires caution.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching does not set prayer and social responsibility against one another: the same Christ whom the believer adores is also present in people in need of help, and faith should shape action in public life. Bearing witness can include courageous dissent, demanding justice, and defending the weak, but also patience, gentleness, or enduring injustice when circumstances prudently require it. Therefore, the most accurate emphasis of the passage is that prayer should lead the believer toward responsible love, not that every form of silence automatically proves unfaithfulness.
concerns_en: The expression “we fit the definition of the lawless” can unfairly generalize various instances of silence: prudence, the protection of others, or a lack of reliable information can affect how and when someone ought to speak. Church teaching encourages defending the weak and seeking justice, but it also recognizes unobtrusive forms of witness and the enduring of injustice out of love for God.

The call to publicly oppose evil should include truthfulness, prudence, and gentleness; criticism that attributes vanity or a desire for fame to others without sufficient basis can cross into unfair judgment.

Speaking of receiving Jesus' passion can be understood in a Catholic manner as a willingness to endure hardships in union with Christ, but not as identifying one's own suffering with Christ's unique redemptive sacrifice.

sections.subtitle_en: Praise without opposing evil and the personal responsibility of public figures
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar speaks about the personal responsibility to use talents for publicly opposing evil
sections.content_en:
Grebenar dedicates the final section of this iteration to piety that does not translate into action. If believers raise their hands, praise Jesus, and organize spiritual retreats where “everything is nice,” while at the same time remaining silent about evil that has become public and not daring to oppose it publicly, then, he says, **“we fit the definition of the lawless.”** Silence is kept in the face of lawlessness, while “over here we supposedly praise Jesus,” even if that be the prayer of the Rosary in the square or activity in prayer communities.

He also applies this responsibility to himself. He states that he leads a prayer community that he claims is currently **the largest prayer community in the world that prays and fasts every day**. He describes it as the fruit of authentic **Međugorje spirituality** in which people learn to pray the Rosary and meditate on Sacred Scripture, “even if some gnash their teeth at that.”

The fact that so many people listen to him he attributes to God's grace, and not to his own intellect, because the Lord granted him the ability to interpret Sacred Scripture. He emphasizes, however, that there is a part that depends solely on him. “Personally I, Vladimir Grebenar,” he says, choose by free will whether I will use the talents God gave me to expose evil and oppose it. He is ready, he conveys, to be struck by “the whips that struck Jesus,” since he already prays “give me a share of your passion and suffering.” Whoever prays like that, he adds, should not be a hypocrite, but should oppose evil publicly.

### Call to politicians, entrepreneurs, and the clergy

He explicitly directs the message to all who operate in the public sphere:

- **politicians**,
- **entrepreneurs**,
- **leaders of prayer communities**,
- **public figures from the clergy**.

They are expected, he says, to **confront evil publicly**. He sharply criticizes those who instead attack precisely those who do so, while remaining themselves “nicely within four walls, where there is a good meal.” Such people then, according to his description, appear on television and social media “so they can be seen,” because their “five minutes of fame have arrived.”
