sections.subtitle: Strah od Božjeg suda: „Gle koliko ljudi nije spašeno zbog tvoje šutnje“
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar govori o strahu da bi mu Bog mogao reći „bezakoniče“ zbog šutnje i pasivnosti
sections.content:
Nastavljajući tumačenje psalma „Blago svakome koji se boji Gospodina“, voditelj **Vladimir Grebenar** opisuje vlastiti strah pred Bogom. Ne boji se kazne, nego Božjeg prijekora. Grebenar priznaje da se jako boji da mu Gospodin jednoga dana ne kaže: **„Bezakoniče, koliki broj ljudi sam poslao da sluša ono zbog čeg sam ti milost dao, a što si ti učinio?“**

U tom zamišljenom Božjem prijekoru on nabraja što bi mu se moglo predbaciti: da mnogi ljudi nisu spašeni zbog njegove šutnje, da je zlo prodrlo ondje gdje je mogao i trebao imati utjecaj, te da je neprijatelj mnogo toga učinio zbog njegove **šutnje, pasivnosti i nerada**. Kao poseban grijeh navodi i **„naslikavanje po društvenim mrežama“** te objave koje, kako kaže, „veze s vezom nemaju“.

Tom mišlju Grebenar zaokružuje prethodni dio tumačenja. U njemu je tvrdio da vjernik koji javno moli i slavi Boga, a šuti pred zlom koje je postalo javno, po njegovu mišljenju odgovara evanđeoskoj definiciji bezakonika.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv da kršćanin ne šuti pred zlom i da odgovorno naviješta evanđelje u skladu je s katoličkim naglaskom na misijskom poslanju i odgovornosti za druge. Ipak, govor prelazi u teološki rizičnu pretpostavku kada se tvrdi da su mnogi ljudi „zbog tvoje šutnje“ ostali nespašeni ili se zamišljeni prijekor prikazuje kao određena Božja presuda pojedincu, a javna molitva uz šutnju pred zlom naziva se bezakonjem bez potrebnog konteksta.
concerns: Izraz „mnogi ljudi nisu spašeni zbog tvoje šutnje“ može neopravdano pripisati jednoj osobi određenu uzročnu odgovornost za tuđe konačno spasenje. Kršćanin može imati obvezu svjedočiti i upozoriti, ali iz opisa se ne može zaključiti da bi baš njegova šutnja odredila nečije spasenje.

Nazivanje takve osobe „bezakonikom“ može biti pretjerano ako se ne razlikuju propust, okolnosti i konkretna odgovornost; također se ne može zaključiti da su objave na društvenim mrežama same po sebi grijeh bez poznavanja njihova sadržaja i namjere.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički izvori potvrđuju da navještaj evanđelja nije neobvezan te upozoravaju da šutnja pastira pred zabludom može biti štetna; Benedikt XVI. također ističe kako se pred nepravdom ei ne smije ostati ravnodušan, nego treba živjeti odgovornošću za vlastito i tuđe spasenje. No isti naglasak treba izreći s razboritošću: poziv na hrabro svjedočenje nije ovlast da se bez dostatnog znanja proglasi tko je kriv za tuđi gubitak spasenja ili kakvu će presudu Bog izreći.

citations.document_title: 12 September 2006: Holy Mass at Islinger Feld in Regensburg

magisterium.assessment_en: The call for a Christian not to remain silent before evil and to responsibly proclaim the Gospel is in accordance with the Catholic emphasis on the missionary mission and responsibility for others. However, the discourse crosses into a theologically risky assumption when it is claimed that many people remained unsaved „because of your silence“ or an imagined reproach is presented as a definite judgment of God upon an individual, and public prayer accompanied by silence before evil is called lawlessness without the necessary context.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic sources confirm that the proclamation of the Gospel is not optional and warn that the silence of pastors before error can be harmful; Benedict XVI also emphasizes that in the face of injustice one must not remain indifferent, but should live with responsibility for one's own and others' salvation. However, the same emphasis must be expressed with prudence: the call to courageous witnessing is not an authorization to declare, without sufficient knowledge, who is to blame for someone else's loss of salvation or what judgment God will pronounce.
concerns_en: The expression „many people were not saved because of your silence“ can unjustifiably attribute to one person a definite causal responsibility for someone else's final salvation. A Christian may have an obligation to witness and warn, but from the description it cannot be concluded that his silence specifically would determine someone's salvation.

Calling such a person a „lawless one“ can be excessive if omission, circumstances, and concrete responsibility are not distinguished; likewise, it cannot be concluded that posts on social media are inherently a sin without knowing their content and intention.

sections.subtitle_en: Fear of God's judgment: „Look how many people were not saved because of your silence“
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar speaks about the fear that God might say „lawless one“ to him because of silence and passivity
sections.content_en:
Continuing the interpretation of the psalm „Blessed is everyone who fears the Lord“, host **Vladimir Grebenar** describes his own fear before God. He does not fear punishment, but God's reproach. Grebenar admits that he is very afraid that one day the Lord might say to him: **„Lawless one, how many people did I send to listen to that for which I gave you grace, and what did you do?“**

In that imagined God's reproach, he lists what could be reproached to him: that many people were not saved because of his silence, that evil penetrated where he could and should have had an influence, and that the enemy did many things because of his **silence, passivity, and inactivity**. As a particular sin he also cites **„posing for pictures on social media“** and posts that, as he says, „have nothing to do with anything“.

With that thought, Grebenar rounds off the previous part of the interpretation. In it, he claimed that a believer who publicly prays and praises God, but is silent before evil that has become public, in his opinion corresponds to the Gospel definition of a lawless person.

sections.subtitle: Više žalosti za slavnim pjevačem nego na Veliki petak
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj kritizira javno žalovanje za slavnim osobama na društvenim mrežama
sections.content:
Kao konkretan primjer neprimjerenih objava Grebenar navodi slučaj kad umre neki narodni pjevač ili omiljeni glumac koji nije katolik. To može biti pripadnik druge religije ili drugog naroda, ili netko tko je kršten, ali nije vjernik. Za takvom se osobom, primjećuje voditelj, po društvenim mrežama danima žali, **„čak i od strane nekih koji su u kleru“**.

Citiraju se njezine riječi iz serija ili stihovi pjesama. Grebenar pritom ističe da ni ti filmovi, ni serije, ni glazba nisu proslavljali Isusa, nego su bili „za narodne mase“. Njegov zaključak je oštar: **više je žalosti kad umre neki narodni heroj nego na Veliki petak.**

Posebno ga je pogodila objava u kojoj netko za preminulim piše: **„Bili smo prijatelji.“** Na to se pita: „Kako se Boga ne bojiš to pisati po društvenim mrežama? Bio si prijatelj s nekim tko nije kršćanin.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak opravdano upozorava da se javno žalovanje može pretvoriti u pretjerano veličanje neke osobe, ali njegov prijekor zbog žalosti za pokojnikom koji nije kršćanin i zbog tvrdnje da mu je netko bio prijatelj znatno odstupa od kršćanske osjetljivosti. Isus je plakao za svojim prijateljem Lazarom, a katoličko učenje priznaje žalost za umrlima kao prirodnu i dopuštenu, neovisno o tome pripada li pokojnik kršćanskoj zajednici.
concerns: Pitanje „Kako se Boga ne bojiš?” može sugerirati da je prijateljstvo s nekršćaninom samo po sebi grešno ili sramotno; odlomak ne daje osnovu za takvu tvrdnju.
Usporedba žalovanja za javnom osobom s Velikim petkom može posramiti ljude zbog iskrene tuge, premda kršćanska nada u uskrsnuće ne ukida ljudsku bol zbog smrti.

Procjena pokojnika prema tome jesu li njegova djela „proslavljala Isusa” ne dokazuje da je žalovanje za njim neprimjereno; važna je razlika između tuge za osobom i nekritičkog prihvaćanja njezina života ili djela.
magisterium.enrichment: Ivanovo evanđelje prikazuje Isusa kako se potresa i plače uz Lazarov grob, a Međunarodna teologijska komisija izričito kaže da možemo i trebamo plakati za umrlima koje volimo. Katolički pristup zato može istodobno čuvati kršćansku nadu i poštovati žalost, prijateljstvo i ljudsko dostojanstvo pokojnika; pastoralna pratnja treba biti strpljiva i prilagođena osobi koja tuguje.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage reasonably warns that public mourning can turn into excessive glorification of a person, but its reproach over grief for a deceased person who is not a Christian and over claiming that someone was their friend departs significantly from Christian sensibility. Jesus wept for his friend Lazarus, and Catholic teaching recognizes grief for the dead as natural and permissible, regardless of whether the deceased belonged to the Christian community.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Gospel of John depicts Jesus being moved and weeping at Lazarus's tomb, and the International Theological Commission explicitly states that we can and should weep for the dead we love. Therefore, a Catholic approach can simultaneously preserve Christian hope and respect grief, friendship, and the human dignity of the deceased; pastoral accompaniment should be patient and tailored to the grieving person.
concerns_en: The question “How do you not fear God?” may suggest that friendship with a non-Christian is inherently sinful or shameful; the passage provides no basis for such a claim.
Comparing mourning for a public figure with Good Friday may shame people for sincere sorrow, even though Christian hope in the resurrection does not eliminate human pain over death.

Evaluating the deceased based on whether their works “glorified Jesus” does not prove that mourning for them is inappropriate; the distinction between sorrow for a person and uncritical acceptance of their life or work is important.

sections.subtitle_en: More grief for a famous singer than on Good Friday
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host criticizes public mourning for celebrities on social media
sections.content_en:
As a concrete example of inappropriate posts, Grebenar cites the case when a folk singer or a beloved actor who is not Catholic dies. This could be a member of another religion or another nation, or someone who is baptized, but is not a believer. For such a person, the host notes, people grieve on social media for days, **“even on the part of some who are in the clergy.”**

Their words from series or song lyrics are quoted. Grebenar at the same time emphasizes that neither those movies, nor series, nor music glorified Jesus, but were “for the masses.” His conclusion is sharp: **there is more grief when a folk hero dies than on Good Friday.**

He was especially struck by a post in which someone writes about the deceased: **“We were friends.”** To that he asks: “How do you not fear God writing that on social media? You were friends with someone who is not a Christian.”

sections.subtitle: „Bili smo prijatelji“: prijateljstvo koje obvezuje na navještaj
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar postavlja pitanje može li kršćanin zvati prijateljem nekoga kome nije navijestio Krista
sections.content:
Grebenar prelazi na pitanje prijateljstva s pripadnicima drugih religija. Pitanje upućuje svima, a osobito pripadnicima klera. Za njih kaže da bi trebali **„živjeti za Isusa, a ne od Isusa“**. Pita: ako netko ima prijatelja budista, hindusa, muslimana ili ateista i zove ga prijateljem, je li mu Isus doista prijatelj ili to tvrdi samo deklarativno?

Prema njegovu tumačenju, Isus je išao na križ da bi svi postali kršćani katolici i da bi se **„svako koljeno nebesnika, zemnika i podzemnika prignulo“** te priznalo da je Isus Krist Gospodin. Stoga pita je li taj prijatelj kleknuo pred križ i rekao „Ti si Sin Božji“. Možda je umjesto toga samo nudio novac. Kao primjere navodi bogatog hindusa koji oprema katoličku bolnicu, vlasnika kladionice koji oprema crkvu ili nekome od svećenika kupuje automobil.

Ako kršćanin ima prijatelja koji ne prigiba koljena pred Isusom, ne zastaje pred križem, ne ide na misu i ne prima tijelo Kristovo, a nije mu navijestio Krista, Grebenar zaključuje da je takav kršćanin **„totalno zastranio“**. Po njegovim riječima, tada je „gori od najgorih farizeja koji su razapeli Isusa“ i „veća kukavica od apostola koji su pobjegli ispod križa“.

Njegovo je načelo jasno: **„Ako ti nekog zoveš svojim prijateljem, onda tebe to obvezuje da mu navijestiš Krista. To je kršćanstvo na djelu.“** Bez toga, tvrdi, prijateljstva nema.

magisterium.assessment: Ispravno naglašava da kršćanin treba svjedočiti Kristu i da međureligijski dijalog ne isključuje navještaj evanđelja, ali pogrešno prikazuje prijateljstvo kao da ovisi o tome je li prijatelj već prihvatio vjeru. Osuda da je vjernik bez takva navještaja „gori“ od farizeja ili apostola koji su pobjegli neopravdano je oštra i ne odražava crkveni poziv na razborito, strpljivo i poštovano svjedočenje.
concerns: Tvrdnja da je Isus išao na križ „da bi svi postali kršćani katolici“ previše izravno poistovjećuje Kristovo univerzalno spasenjsko djelo s tvrdnjom da svi moraju za života postati vidljivi članovi Katoličke Crkve; priloženi izvori podupiru Kristovo jedinstveno posredništvo i poslanje naviještanja, ali ne tu formulaciju.

Postavljanje navještaja kao uvjeta za istinsko prijateljstvo može narušiti poštovanje slobode i dostojanstva osobe. Crkveni nauk traži svjedočenje bez prisile, uz slušanje, poštovanje i razlučivanje što je u pojedinoj situaciji primjereno.
Primjeri financijske pomoći sami po sebi ne pokazuju da osoba nije prijatelj ili da kršćanin zanemaruje vjeru; Crkva izričito potiče korisnu suradnju među pripadnicima različitih zajednica.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk drži zajedno dvije istine: Krist je jedini Spasitelj, a kršćani su obvezani naviještati ga; pritom su dijalog i navještaj povezani, a ne suprotstavljeni. Prijateljstvo može biti mjesto radosnog i iskrenog svjedočenja, ali ono uključuje i slušanje, poštovanje uvjerenja drugoga te strpljenje prema vremenu i načinu na koji osoba odgovara.

citations.document_title: The Attitude of the Church towards the Followers of Other Religions: Reflections and Orientations on Dialogue and Mission
To participants in the Plenary Assembly of the Pontifical Council for Interreligious Dialogue (28 November 2013)
Christian witness in a multi-religious world
To the members of the non-Catholic and other religious communities in Kigali (September 9, 1990) - Speech

magisterium.assessment_en: It correctly emphasizes that a Christian ought to bear witness to Christ and that interreligious dialogue does not exclude the proclamation of the Gospel, but it mistakenly portrays friendship as depending on whether the friend has already accepted the faith. The condemnation that a believer without such proclamation is “worse” than the Pharisees or the apostles who fled is unjustifiably harsh and does not reflect the Church's call to prudent, patient, and respectful witnessing.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching holds together two truths: Christ is the only Savior, and Christians are obliged to proclaim Him; at the same time, dialogue and proclamation are connected, not opposed. Friendship can be a place of joyful and sincere witnessing, but it also includes listening, respect for the convictions of the other, and patience toward the time and manner in which the person responds.
concerns_en: The claim that Jesus went to the cross “so that all would become Catholic Christians” too directly equates Christ's universal salvific work with the claim that all must become visible members of the Catholic Church during their lifetime; the attached sources support Christ's unique mediation and the mission of proclamation, but not this formulation.

Setting proclamation as a condition for true friendship can undermine respect for the freedom and dignity of the person. Church teaching calls for witnessing without coercion, along with listening, respect, and discernment of what is appropriate in an individual situation.

Examples of financial assistance do not in themselves demonstrate that a person is not a friend or that a Christian is neglecting the faith; the Church explicitly encourages fruitful cooperation among members of different communities.

sections.subtitle_en: “We Were Friends”: Friendship That Obliges to Proclamation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar poses the question of whether a Christian can call a friend someone to whom he has not proclaimed Christ
sections.content_en:
Grebenar moves on to the question of friendship with members of other religions. He directs the question to everyone, and especially to members of the clergy. About them he says that they should **“live for Jesus, not off of Jesus”**. He asks: if someone has a Buddhist, Hindu, Muslim, or atheist friend and calls him a friend, is Jesus truly his friend or does he claim that merely declaratively?

According to his interpretation, Jesus went to the cross so that all would become Catholic Christians and that **“every knee should bend, of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth”** and confess that Jesus Christ is Lord. Therefore he asks whether that friend has knelt before the cross and said “You are the Son of God”. Perhaps instead he was merely offering money. As examples he cites a wealthy Hindu who equips a Catholic hospital, a betting shop owner who equips a church or buys a car for one of the priests.

If a Christian has a friend who does not bend his knees before Jesus, does not pause before the cross, does not go to Mass, and does not receive the body of Christ, and he has not proclaimed Christ to him, Grebenar concludes that such a Christian has **“totally gone astray”**. In his words, he is then “worse than the worst Pharisees who crucified Jesus” and “a bigger coward than the apostles who fled from under the cross”.

His principle is clear: **“If you call someone your friend, then that obliges you to proclaim Christ to him. That is Christianity in action.”** Without that, he claims, there is no friendship.

sections.subtitle: Jedna rečenica na poslovnom ručku i primjer Majke Tereze
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj navodi primjer Majke Tereze koja je liječila hinduse
sections.content:
Grebenar razlikuje prijateljstvo od kolegijalnog odnosa. S ljudima drugih religija moguće je biti korektan po ljudskim i etičkim standardima, primjerice zbog posla sjesti s njima na ručak. On sam kaže da ima takvo iskustvo. No i u takvim susretima, ističe, Bog nekoga može poslati da mu se posvjedoči. Čovjek možda nikad nije čuo za Isusa, a **„dovoljna je jedna rečenica“**.

To vrijedi i za politiku, gdje se ljudi susreću s onima drugih religija i svjetonazora. Autentični kršćanin dužan je posvjedočiti barem jednom rečenicom da je Kristov. Može to učiniti i znakom, primjerice tako da se **prekriži prije jela** pred sugovornikom. Onome tko druge zove prijateljima, a pritom se predstavlja kao „Kristov laik“ ili „Kristov svećenik“, Grebenar poručuje da ga otkrivaju djela.

Navještaj se, prema voditelju, može dati riječju ili ljubavlju, **kao Majka Tereza**. Ona je liječila i prihvaćala hinduse, a oni su po njoj upoznavali Isusa. Grebenar zatim oblikuje svjedočanstvo kakvo bi vjernik trebao uputiti prijatelju: da je Isus Krist put, da nema drugog spasenja ni drugih spasitelja i da je Isus umro za njega. Dodaje da ga Isus možda ljubi i više nego samog vjernika te da za njegovom dušom žudi. **„Žedan je Isus. Žedan je obraćenja ljudi“**, naglašava voditelj. Kad čovjek tako čuje svjedočanstvo izrečeno iz srca, može se obratiti i reći: „Ja se želim krstiti.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: potvrđuje Krista kao jedinog Spasitelja i važnost naviještanja riječju i djelima, uključujući svjedočanstvo kroz ljubav prema ljudima drugih religija. Ipak, tvrdnje da je „dovoljna jedna rečenica” i da je svaki kršćanin dužan svjedočiti baš barem jednom rečenicom mogu zvučati previše shematski ako zanemare slobodu sugovornika, razboritost i činjenicu da obraćenje nije u ljudskoj kontroli.
concerns: Izraz „nema drugog spasenja ni drugih spasitelja” u katoličkom je smislu prihvatljiv ako jasno znači da je Krist jedini izvor i posrednik spasenja; ne bi ga trebalo razumjeti kao tvrdnju da Bog ne može spasiti osobe koje bez vlastite krivnje nisu upoznale Evanđelje.
„Dovoljna je jedna rečenica” može značiti da i kratak iskren iskaz može biti važan početak svjedočenja, ali ne jamči obraćenje niti zamjenjuje daljnji odnos, katehezu i sakramentalni život.
Svjedočenje prekrižiti se prije jela može biti prikladan, nenametljiv znak vjere, no ne treba ga pretvoriti u obveznu formulu za svaki susret ili mjerilo autentičnosti kršćanina.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva istodobno potvrđuje odgovornost kršćana da svjedoče Kristu i uči da je obraćenje naposljetku djelo Duha Svetoga, a ne nešto što čovjek može proizvesti ili zajamčiti. Isključivost Kristova spasenja zato ne opravdava prisilu: svjedočanstvo treba biti slobodno i vođeno ljubavlju, dok se osobe koje bez vlastite krivnje ne poznaju Evanđelje povjeravaju Božjem spasenjskom djelovanju. Primjer Majke Tereze dobro pokazuje da se Evanđelje može naviještati i djelima samilosne ljubavi, ali takva djela nisu zamjena za Krista nego svjedočanstvo njegove ljubavi.

citations.document_title: Christian witness in a multi-religious world
Madre Teresa di Calcutta (1910-1997) - Apostolic letter
4 February 1986, Mass for Catholics of West Bengala (Calcutta)

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: it affirms Christ as the only Savior and the importance of proclamation by word and deeds, including witness through love towards people of other religions. Nevertheless, the assertions that "one sentence is enough" and that every Christian is obliged to witness with at least one sentence can sound overly schematic if they disregard the freedom of the interlocutor, prudence, and the fact that conversion is not under human control.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church simultaneously affirms the responsibility of Christians to witness to Christ and teaches that conversion is ultimately the work of the Holy Spirit, not something that man can produce or guarantee. The exclusivity of Christ's salvation therefore does not justify coercion: witnessing should be free and guided by love, while persons who through no fault of their own do not know the Gospel are entrusted to God's salvific action. The example of Mother Teresa demonstrates well that the Gospel can also be proclaimed through deeds of compassionate love, but such deeds are not a substitute for Christ, but rather a testimony of His love.
concerns_en: The expression "there is no other salvation nor other saviors" is acceptable in the Catholic sense if it clearly means that Christ is the only source and mediator of salvation; it should not be understood as an assertion that God cannot save persons who, through no fault of their own, have not come to know the Gospel.

"One sentence is enough" can mean that even a short, sincere statement can be an important beginning of witnessing, but it does not guarantee conversion nor replace a further relationship, catechesis, and sacramental life.

Witnessing by making the sign of the cross before eating can be a suitable, unobtrusive sign of faith, but it should not be turned into a mandatory formula for every encounter or a measure of a Christian's authenticity.

sections.subtitle_en: One sentence at a business lunch and the example of Mother Teresa
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host cites the example of Mother Teresa who treated Hindus
sections.content_en:
Grebenar distinguishes friendship from a collegial relationship. With people of other religions, it is possible to be correct according to human and ethical standards, for example sitting down to lunch with them because of work. He himself says that he has such an experience. Yet even in such encounters, he points out, God can send someone so that testimony may be given to him. A person may have never heard of Jesus, and **"one sentence is enough"**.

This also applies to politics, where people encounter those of other religions and worldviews. An authentic Christian is obliged to witness with at least one sentence that he is Christ's. He can also do this with a sign, for example by **making the sign of the cross before eating** in front of his interlocutor. To someone who calls others friends, while at the same time presenting himself as "Christ's layman" or "Christ's priest", Grebenar says that his deeds reveal him.

Proclamation, according to the host, can be given by word or by love, **like Mother Teresa**. She treated and accepted Hindus, and through her they came to know Jesus. Grebenar then forms a testimony such as a believer should address to a friend: that Jesus Christ is the way, that there is no other salvation nor other saviors, and that Jesus died for him. He adds that Jesus perhaps loves him even more than the believer himself and that He yearns for his soul. **"Jesus is thirsty. He is thirsty for the conversion of people"**, emphasizes the host. When a person thus hears a testimony spoken from the heart, he can convert and say: "I want to be baptized."

sections.subtitle: Kad prijatelj odbije: „Ti si u zabludi“, i teškoće mješovitih brakova
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar objašnjava zašto se sakramentalni brakovi s pripadnicima drugih religija teško održe
sections.content:
Što ako takozvani prijatelj odgovori da poštuje njegovo uvjerenje, ali da je kršćanstvo „samo jedna od ponuda“, a on kao hindus, budist ili musliman ima svoje? Grebenar odgovara da je vjernik tada dužan reći mu: **„Gle, ti si u zabludi.“**

Kao usporedbu navodi praksu Katoličke Crkve u pitanju braka. Da bi primili sakrament vjenčanja, muškarac i žena trebaju biti katolici. Voditelj spominje i iznimke, kad je jedna strana druge religije, ali smatra da se takvi savezi **„u pravilu raspadaju vrlo brzo“**. Civilni brak može trajati desetljećima, no ustrajanje u sakramentalnom životu, kaže, „jako je rijetko“. Jedna strana prevlada, druga se mora prilagoditi ili brak pukne. Priznaje da ni sam nije čuo za suprotan slučaj.

Zato, poručuje, treba biti potpuno izravan i govoriti istinu onako kako je zapisana u Svetom pismu, bez priča o „progresu“ svijeta. Ironično se osvrće na Francusku, „zemlju prosvjetiteljstva, znanosti, napretka“, i na prizore mladih iz Pariza. „Bože nas sačuvaj takvih mladih u hrvatskom narodu“, kaže. Ako bi takva bila mladost u Hrvatskoj, zaključuje, „neće više biti Hrvatske“.

magisterium.assessment: Dužnost svjedočiti Kristu i ne razvodnjavati Evanđelje u skladu je s kršćanskim poslanjem, ali izravan navještaj ne opravdava omalovažavajući odnos prema sugovorniku niti neprovjerene tvrdnje o mješovitim brakovima. Tvrdnja da oba supružnika moraju biti katolici kako bi brak bio sakrament te da se mješoviti brakovi u pravilu brzo raspadaju nije u skladu s crkvenim razlikovanjima i pastoralnim naukom.
concerns: Katolički nauk razlikuje brak katolika s krštenim nekatolikom od braka katolika s nekrštenom osobom; brak krštenih osoba može biti sakrament i kada jedan supružnik nije katolik, pa tvrdnja da oboje moraju biti katolici nije točna.

Crkva upozorava na stvarne teškoće mješovitih brakova, osobito u pogledu vjerskog života i odgoja djece, ali kaže da se teškoće mogu prevladavati pastoralnom skrbi; kategorička tvrdnja da se takvi brakovi „u pravilu raspadaju vrlo brzo” nije potkrijepljena navedenim naučnim izvorima.

Poziv „ti si u zabludi” može izražavati neslaganje s uvjerenjem, ali bez poštovanja i objašnjenja riskira da navještaj zamijeni grubim etiketiranjem; kršćansko svjedočenje uključuje naviještanje Krista, a ne prisilu ili prezir prema osobi.
Ironično omalovažavanje mladih i povezivanje njihova stanja s nestankom Hrvatske nije teološki argument i može zanemariti dostojanstvo osoba; dostupni izvori ne daju osnovu za takvu generalizaciju.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva ne izjednačuje sve vrste mješovitih brakova: u braku katolika i krštenog nekatolika postoji sakramentalna veza ako je brak valjan, dok se brak s nekrštenom osobom razlikuje po naravi i sakramentalnom statusu. Pavao u 1 Kor 7,12–13 upućuje da vjernik ne treba napustiti supružnika koji pristaje ostati u braku, a crkveni biblijski dokument naglašava uzajamno poštovanje i zajedničko odlučivanje o djeci. Zato iskreno svjedočenje katoličke istine treba spojiti s razboritim govorom, poštovanjem sugovornika i pastoralnom brigom za parove.

magisterium.assessment_en: The duty to witness to Christ and not dilute the Gospel is in accordance with the Christian mission, but direct proclamation does not justify a disparaging attitude toward an interlocutor nor unverified claims about mixed marriages. The claim that both spouses must be Catholic for a marriage to be a sacrament and that mixed marriages as a rule fall apart quickly is not in accordance with the Church's distinctions and pastoral teaching.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church does not equate all types of mixed marriages: in a marriage of a Catholic and a baptized non-Catholic there is a sacramental bond if the marriage is valid, while a marriage with an unbaptized person differs in nature and sacramental status. Paul in 1 Cor 7:12–13 instructs that a believer should not leave a spouse who consents to remain in the marriage, and an ecclesial biblical document emphasizes mutual respect and joint decision-making regarding children. Therefore, sincere witnessing to Catholic truth should be joined with prudent speech, respect for the interlocutor, and pastoral care for couples.
concerns_en: Catholic teaching distinguishes the marriage of a Catholic with a baptized non-Catholic from the marriage of a Catholic with an unbaptized person; the marriage of baptized persons can be a sacrament even when one spouse is not Catholic, so the claim that both must be Catholics is not accurate.

The Church warns of the real difficulties of mixed marriages, especially regarding religious life and the upbringing of children, but states that difficulties can be overcome through pastoral care; the categorical claim that such marriages "as a rule fall apart very quickly" is not substantiated by the cited doctrinal sources.

The statement "you are in error" can express disagreement with a conviction, but without respect and explanation it risks replacing proclamation with harsh labeling; Christian witness includes proclaiming Christ, not coercion or contempt toward the person.

Ironic disparagement of youth and linking their condition with the disappearance of Croatia is not a theological argument and can disregard the dignity of persons; the available sources provide no basis for such a generalization.

sections.subtitle_en: When a friend rejects: "You are in error", and the difficulties of mixed marriages
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar explains why sacramental marriages with members of other religions are difficult to sustain
sections.content_en:
What if a so-called friend responds that he respects his belief, but that Christianity is "just one of the offerings", while he, as a Hindu, Buddhist, or Muslim, has his own? Grebenar answers that the believer is then obliged to tell him: **"Look, you are in error."**

As a comparison, he cites the practice of the Catholic Church regarding marriage. In order to receive the sacrament of marriage, a man and a woman need to be Catholics. The host also mentions exceptions, when one party is of another religion, but considers that such unions **"as a rule fall apart very quickly"**. A civil marriage can last for decades, but persevering in sacramental life, he says, is "very rare". One party prevails, the other must adapt, or the marriage breaks down. He admits that he himself has not heard of an opposite case.

Therefore, he conveys, one should be completely direct and speak the truth as it is written in Sacred Scripture, without stories of the "progress" of the world. He ironically reflects on France, the "land of the Enlightenment, science, progress", and on the scenes of young people from Paris. "God save us from such young people in the Croatian nation", he says. If youth in Croatia were to be like that, he concludes, "there will no longer be a Croatia".

sections.subtitle: Isusove posljednje riječi kao zapovijed na vratima svakog doma
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj naglašava težinu Isusovih posljednjih riječi prije uzašašća
sections.content:
Sve proizlazi iz straha Božjega, naglašava Grebenar. Tko se boji Boga, navijestit će Krista „takozvanom prijatelju“, a on će sam odlučiti hoće li Isusa prihvatiti ili odbaciti. Za mjerilo voditelj ne uzima mišljenja „nekih bibličara i liberalnih teologa“, nego Isusove vlastite riječi, i to one posljednje, izrečene pred uzašašće.

Težinu posljednjih riječi ilustrira osobnim iskustvom. Sjeća se posljednjih riječi svoje pokojne bake prije nego što je izdahnula: „To sam svojim očima vidio, to se ne zaboravlja.“ Podsjeća i kako svi pozorno slušaju mladence kad se na svadbi obraćaju gostima, ili umirućega kad se oprašta od bližnjih.

Isusove posljednje riječi, smatra Grebenar, trebale bi **„pisati na svim ulazima u sve stambene zgrade, u stanove, u kuće“**, jer nisu pozdravne, nego su zapovijed. Isus se, objašnjava, ne oprašta od učenika, nego kaže: „Ostajem s vama u sve dane do svršetka svijeta. Neću vas ostaviti siročad.“ Odlazi u tijelu, ali se vraća kroz euharistiju i na druge načine. S prijestolja slave milost dolazi u euharistiju, ispovijed i Crkvu, po rukama svećenika.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak uglavnom izražava katoličko razumijevanje Kristova misijskog naloga, trajne prisutnosti s Crkvom i Euharistije kao sakramenta njegove prisutnosti. Ipak, spaja različite evanđeoske izreke i neprecizno opisuje Kristovu prisutnost nakon Uzašašća kao njegov „povratak“ kroz Euharistiju.
concerns: Tvrdnja da Isus ne ostavlja učenike siročadima („Neću vas ostaviti siročad“) nije dio Mt 28,20, nego je ovdje spojena s riječima „Ja sam s vama u sve dane do svršetka svijeta“. Time se može zamagliti razlika između različitih Isusovih govora i evanđeoskih odlomaka.

Izraz da Isus odlazi u tijelu, ali se „vraća kroz euharistiju“ može zvučati kao da je nakon Uzašašća odsutan pa se ponovno vraća. Preciznije je reći da Krist uzašavši ne napušta svijet te da je u Euharistiji sakramentalno i stvarno prisutan; Euharistija je osobito snažna potvrda njegova obećanja „Ja sam s vama“.

Navještaj se povezuje sa strahom Božjim, ali bez dodatnog objašnjenja taj izraz može značiti ili sinovsko strahopoštovanje ili strah koji sputava. Odlomak također može ostaviti dojam da je navještaj samo iznošenje ponude nakon čega je svejedno kako se slušaoca prati; Isusov nalog uključuje stvaranje učenika, krštenje i poučavanje svemu što je zapovjedio.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusove riječi prije Uzašašća obuhvaćaju i poslanje Crkve i njegovo obećanje trajne prisutnosti: učenici trebaju naviještati, krštavati i poučavati, a Krist ostaje s njima do svršetka svijeta. Katolički nauk posebno prepoznaje Euharistiju kao sakrament Kristove prisutnosti, ali ona ne iscrpljuje sve načine na koje Krist ostaje prisutan i djelatan u Crkvi.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage generally expresses the Catholic understanding of Christ's missionary mandate, lasting presence with the Church, and the Eucharist as the sacrament of his presence. However, it combines different evangelical sayings and imprecisely describes Christ's presence after the Ascension as his "return" through the Eucharist.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' words before the Ascension encompass both the mission of the Church and his promise of lasting presence: the disciples are to proclaim, baptize, and teach, and Christ remains with them until the end of the world. Catholic teaching particularly recognizes the Eucharist as the sacrament of Christ's presence, but it does not exhaust all the ways in which Christ remains present and active in the Church.
concerns_en: The assertion that Jesus does not leave the disciples orphans ("I will not leave you orphans") is not part of Mt 28:20, but is here merged with the words "I am with you all days until the end of the world." This may blur the distinction between different discourses of Jesus and evangelical passages.

The expression that Jesus departs in the body, but "returns through the Eucharist" may sound as if he is absent after the Ascension and then returns anew. It is more precise to say that Christ, having ascended, does not abandon the world and that in the Eucharist he is sacramentally and truly present; the Eucharist is a particularly powerful confirmation of his promise "I am with you."

The proclamation is linked to the fear of God, but without additional explanation this expression may mean either filial reverence or an inhibiting fear. The passage may also leave the impression that proclamation is merely presenting an offer after which it does not matter how the listener is accompanied; Jesus' mandate includes making disciples, baptizing, and teaching everything he commanded.

sections.subtitle_en: Jesus' last words as a commandment at the doors of every home
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host emphasizes the weight of Jesus' last words before the ascension
sections.content_en:
Everything stems from the fear of God, Grebenar emphasizes. Whoever fears God will proclaim Christ to a "so-called friend," and he will decide for himself whether he will accept or reject Jesus. As a benchmark, the host does not take the opinions of "some biblicists and liberal theologians," but Jesus' own words, and specifically the last ones, spoken before the ascension.

He illustrates the weight of last words with a personal experience. He remembers the last words of his late grandmother before she drew her last breath: "I saw that with my own eyes, that is not forgotten." He also recalls how everyone listens attentively to the newlyweds when they address the guests at a wedding, or to a dying person when saying goodbye to loved ones.

Jesus' last words, Grebenar believes, should **"be written at all entrances to all residential buildings, into apartments, into houses"**, because they are not a farewell greeting, but a commandment. Jesus, he explains, is not saying goodbye to the disciples, but says: "I remain with you all days until the end of the world. I will not leave you orphans." He departs in the body, but returns through the Eucharist and in other ways. From the throne of glory, grace comes into the Eucharist, confession, and the Church, through the hands of priests.

sections.subtitle: „Idite po svem svijetu“: vjera i krštenje kao uvjet spasenja
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar citira Isusovu zapovijed „Idite po svem svijetu i propovijedajte evanđelje“
sections.content:
Središnja zapovijed glasi: **„Idite po svem svijetu i propovijedajte evanđelje.“** Grebenar posebno ističe dva uvjeta za spasenje koja Isus navodi: **povjerovati i pokrstiti se**. Prema njegovu tumačenju, Isus nije rekao da je dovoljno samo povjerovati, a krštenje je sporedno. Tko je povjerovao, mora se i krstiti.

Za one koji ne povjeruju Isus, nastavlja voditelj, kaže samo da će biti osuđeni. Krštenje tu više ne spominje, jer onaj tko nije povjerovao nema ni razloga krstiti se. „O, gle Isusa kako je radikalan, a bio na križu“, primjećuje Grebenar. Dodaje da Isus i Otac nebeski cijene žrtvu na križu, „samo je ne cijene mnogi koji dobro žive od Isusa“.

Na pitanje zašto bi Isus bio tako strog Grebenar odgovara Isusovim riječima: zato što **„nisu povjerovali u jedinorođenoga Sina Božjega“**. „Točka, nema dalje“, zaključuje. Tko nije prignuo koljeno pred Isusom Kristom, prema njegovu tumačenju, ne može se spasiti.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak da Krist zapovijeda naviještanje evanđelja te da su vjera i krštenje povezani s spasenjem u skladu je s Mk 16,16 i katoličkim naukom. Ipak, zaključak da se nitko tko nije izričito ispovjedio vjeru u Krista ne može spasiti izrečen je preapsolutno, a tvrdnja da Isus i Otac „cijene” žrtvu na križu, ali je mnogi iskorištavaju, nije dovoljno razjašnjena.
concerns: Mk 16,16 kaže da će biti spašen onaj koji povjeruje i krsti se, a da će biti osuđen onaj koji ne povjeruje; iz toga ne slijedi da krštenje nije važno, ali ni da se osuda svih koji nisu kršteni može zaključiti bez razlikovanja njihove odgovornosti i okolnosti.

Katolički nauk uči da je krštenje nužno za one kojima je evanđelje naviješteno i koji mogu zatražiti sakrament, ali istodobno kaže da Bog nije vezan sakramentima te da može voditi spasenju one koji bez vlastite krivnje ne poznaju evanđelje. Zato rečenica „ne može se spasiti” treba razlikovati svjesno odbijanje Krista od nekrivog neznanja i drugih okolnosti.

Formulacija „točka, nema dalje” može ostaviti dojam da je spasenje jednostavno presuda zbog neizgovorene vjerske tvrdnje. Katoličko učenje potvrđuje nužnost vjere i Krista, ali također priznaje da Bog poznaje putove kojima može privesti spasenju one koji bez vlastite krivnje nisu upoznali evanđelje.

Optužba da mnogi „dobro žive od Isusa” ne može se procijeniti kao opća tvrdnja bez dodatnog konteksta; ako cilja na licemjerje ili iskorištavanje vjere, trebalo bi je jasno razlikovati od tvrdnje da Kristova žrtva ili njezini plodovi ne vrijede za takve osobe.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva potvrđuje da je krštenje nužno za spasenje onima koji su čuli evanđelje i mogu primiti sakrament; istodobno uči da je Bog sam sebi slobodno ostavio djelovanje izvan vidljivih granica sakramenata. Stoga Mk 16,16 podupire odlučan poziv na vjeru, krštenje i evangelizaciju, ali ne opravdava konačno osuđivanje pojedinaca čiju odgovornost i odnos prema istini poznaje Bog.

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis that Christ commands the proclamation of the gospel and that faith and baptism are connected with salvation is in accordance with Mk 16:16 and Catholic teaching. Nevertheless, the conclusion that no one who has not explicitly professed faith in Christ can be saved is stated too absolutely, and the claim that Jesus and the Father „appreciate” the sacrifice on the cross, but many exploit it, is not sufficiently clarified.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church confirms that baptism is necessary for salvation to those who have heard the gospel and are able to receive the sacrament; at the same time, it teaches that God has freely reserved to Himself action outside the visible boundaries of the sacraments. Therefore, Mk 16:16 supports a decisive call to faith, baptism, and evangelization, but does not justify the definitive condemnation of individuals whose responsibility and relationship to the truth God knows.
concerns_en: Mk 16:16 says that whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned; it does not follow from this that baptism is not important, nor that the condemnation of all who are not baptized can be concluded without distinguishing their responsibility and circumstances.

Catholic teaching teaches that baptism is necessary for those to whom the gospel has been proclaimed and who are able to ask for the sacrament, but at the same time says that God is not bound by the sacraments and that He can lead to salvation those who through no fault of their own do not know the gospel. Therefore, the sentence „cannot be saved” needs to distinguish the conscious rejection of Christ from inculpable ignorance and other circumstances.

The formulation „period, nothing further” can leave the impression that salvation is simply a verdict because of an unstated religious affirmation. Catholic teaching confirms the necessity of faith and Christ, but also acknowledges that God knows ways by which He can lead to salvation those who through no fault of their own have not come to know the gospel.

The accusation that many „live well off Jesus” cannot be assessed as a general claim without additional context; if it targets hypocrisy or the exploitation of faith, it should be clearly distinguished from the claim that Christ's sacrifice or its fruits do not apply to such persons.

sections.subtitle_en: „Go into all the world“: faith and baptism as a condition of salvation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar quotes Jesus' command „Go into all the world and preach the gospel“
sections.content_en:
The central command reads: **„Go into all the world and preach the gospel.“** Grebenar particularly emphasizes two conditions for salvation that Jesus states: **to believe and to be baptized**. According to his interpretation, Jesus did not say that it is enough only to believe, and baptism is secondary. Whoever has believed must also be baptized.

For those who do not believe Jesus, the host continues, says only that they will be condemned. He no longer mentions baptism there, because one who has not believed has no reason to be baptized either. „Oh, look at Jesus, how radical he is, and he was on the cross,“ Grebenar remarks. He adds that Jesus and the Heavenly Father appreciate the sacrifice on the cross, „only many who live well off Jesus do not appreciate it“.

To the question of why Jesus would be so strict Grebenar responds with Jesus' words: because **„they have not believed in the only-begotten Son of God“**. „Period, nothing further“, he concludes. Whoever has not bowed the knee before Jesus Christ, according to his interpretation, cannot be saved.

sections.subtitle: „Kršćanstvo je samo jedna od ponuda“ i samoizopćenje heretika
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj kritizira tezu neimenovanog crkvenog velikodostojnika da je kršćanstvo samo jedna od ponuda
sections.content:
Grebenar zatim oštro kritizira, ne navodeći ime, „vrlo omiljenog crkvenog velikodostojnika“. Za njega kaže da je popularan na lijevo-liberalnim društvenim mrežama i u medijima, a da je izjavio kako je **„kršćanstvo samo jedna od ponuda“**. Takvog velikodostojnika, prema voditelju, slave oni koji su kršteni, ali „nisu upoznali milost Božju“, i suprotstavljaju ga „radikalnima i konzervativnima“.

Voditelj takvu tezu naziva herezom i poručuje da je treba javno i otvoreno raskrinkati, umjesto da se „ljube ručice“ iz poštovanja. Takav pristup, prema njegovu mišljenju, otvara vrata LGBT-u. **„Poštuju se oni koji poštuju Isusa“**, kaže Grebenar. Oni koji ne poštuju jedinorođenoga Sina Božjega i njegov križ, po njegovu tumačenju, **sami su sebe izopćili**, bez obzira na ruho koje nose. „Ne treba ti to nitko ni reći. Naučavaš hereze, zavodiš narod, sam sebe si ekskomunicirao“, kaže, i dodaje da takvih slučajeva ima mnogo.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je usklađen s katoličkim naukom kad odbacuje vjerski relativizam i naglašava jedinstveno spasenjsko značenje Isusa Krista; ako „kršćanstvo je samo jedna od ponuda“ znači da su sve religije jednako istinite ili spasenjski ravnopravne, to bi bilo protivno katoličkom nauku. Međutim, proglašavanje neimenovanog crkvenog velikodostojnika heretikom i tvrdnja da se sam izopćio nisu opravdani bez provjere što je točno naučavao i jesu li ispunjeni uvjeti crkvenog prava.
concerns: Izraz „kršćanstvo je samo jedna od ponuda“ iznesen je bez konteksta: mogao bi označavati indiferentizam, koji Crkva odbacuje, ali sam navod ne omogućuje pouzdanu procjenu što je govornik zapravo tvrdio.

Hereza nije isto što i svaka pogrešna ili nejasna izjava: odnosi se na ustrajno nijekanje ili sumnju u istinu koju treba vjerovati božanskom i katoličkom vjerom. Odlomak ne utvrđuje ni sadržaj navodne zablude ni potrebnu ustrajnost.

Kan. 1364 predviđa izopćenje za heretika, ali se ne može zaključiti da je osoba automatski izopćena samo zato što je voditelj optužuje za krivovjerje; primjenjivost kazne ovisi o tome jesu li doista ispunjeni pravni i činjenični uvjeti.

Tvrdnja da takav pristup „otvara vrata LGBT-u“ nije objašnjena teološkim argumentom, a dostupni kontekst ne pruža osnovu za procjenu te poveznice. Oštar i osoban ton može zamagliti razliku između kritike nauka i osude konkretne osobe.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička vjera ispovijeda Isusa kao jedinoga Spasitelja, a Crkva zato ne smatra da su sve religije jednake u svojim istinosnim zahtjevima; to, međutim, ne isključuje poštovanje drugih ljudi ni prepoznavanje istine i dobra izvan vidljivih granica Crkve. Crkveno razlikovanje važno je i kod optužbe za herezu: treba razmotriti što je osoba doista naučavala, odnosi li se to na istinu koja se mora vjerovati vjerom te je li riječ o ustrajnom nijekanju, a ne naprosto o spornoj formulaciji.
