magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is aligned with Catholic teaching when it rejects religious relativism and emphasizes the unique salvific significance of Jesus Christ; if “Christianity is only one of the offers” means that all religions are equally true or salvifically equal, that would be contrary to Catholic teaching. However, declaring an unnamed church dignitary a heretic and asserting that he has excommunicated himself are not justified without verifying what he accurately taught and whether the requirements of canon law are fulfilled.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic faith professes Jesus as the only Savior, and the Church therefore does not consider that all religions are equal in their truth claims; this, however, does not exclude respect for other people or the recognition of truth and goodness outside the visible boundaries of the Church. Ecclesial discernment is also important in accusations of heresy: one must consider what the person truly taught, whether it pertains to a truth that must be believed by divine and Catholic faith, and whether it is a matter of persistent denial, rather than simply a contentious formulation.
concerns_en: The expression “Christianity is only one of the offers” is presented without context: it could indicate indifferentism, which the Church rejects, but the quotation itself does not allow for a reliable assessment of what the speaker actually asserted.

Heresy is not the same as every mistaken or unclear statement: it refers to the persistent denial or doubt of a truth that must be believed with divine and Catholic faith. The passage establishes neither the content of the alleged error nor the required persistence.

Can. 1364 provides for excommunication for a heretic, but one cannot conclude that a person is automatically excommunicated simply because the host accuses him of heresy; the applicability of the penalty depends on whether the legal and factual conditions are truly fulfilled.

The claim that such an approach “opens the door to LGBT” is not explained by a theological argument, and the available context does not provide a basis for assessing that connection. The sharp and personal tone may obscure the distinction between the critique of teaching and the condemnation of a specific person.

sections.subtitle_en: “Christianity is only one of the offers” and the self-excommunication of heretics
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host criticizes the thesis of an unnamed church dignitary that Christianity is only one of the offers
sections.content_en:
Grebenar then sharply criticizes, without mentioning a name, a “very beloved church dignitary”. He says of him that he is popular on left-liberal social networks and in the media, and that he stated that **“Christianity is only one of the offers”**. Such a dignitary, according to the host, is celebrated by those who are baptized but “have not come to know the grace of God”, and they contrast him with “the radical and conservative”.

The host calls such a thesis heresy and says that it should be publicly and openly exposed, instead of “kissing hands” out of respect. Such an approach, according to his opinion, opens the door to LGBT. **“Those who respect Jesus are respected”**, says Grebenar. Those who do not respect the only-begotten Son of God and his cross, according to his interpretation, **have excommunicated themselves**, regardless of the vestments they wear. “Nobody even needs to tell you that. You teach heresies, you mislead the people, you have excommunicated yourself,” he says, and adds that there are many such cases.

sections.subtitle: Koncerti u korizmi, žalovanje dijela klera i istina u lice farizejima
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar govori o koncertima u korizmi i Velikom tjednu i reakcijama dijela klera
sections.content:
Vraćajući se primjeru preminulog pjevača, Grebenar priznaje da ga je ta situacija zaboljela. Riječ je o omiljenom izvođaču iz drugog naroda i druge religije. Za njega se isticalo da je „pomagao katolicima“, a istodobno je, prema voditelju, održavao koncerte po katoličkim gradovima Hrvatske i Bosne i Hercegovine **za vrijeme korizme, pa čak i u Velikom tjednu**, kad katolici, kako naglašava, ne smiju ići na koncerte.

Grebenar kaže da ga „boli srce“ što su neki iz klera po društvenim mrežama za tim pjevačem iskazivali žalost veću nego za samim Gospodinom na Veliki petak. To su, po njegovim riječima, oni koji objavljuju „lijepe sličice nepoznatih autora“. Takve naziva zavodnicima koji propovijedaju i vode političke emisije, a njihovu duhovnost opisuje kao **„duhovnost zavisti“** koja, prema njegovu tumačenju, nije od Boga.

Na pitanje kako se odnositi prema farizejima odgovara: onako kako je to činio Isus, **„treba im reći istinu u lice, licemjeri“**. Svoju poruku završava pitanjem: „Bojite se svijeta, bojite se đavla, a ne bojite se Gospodina. Pa koji duh te vodi ako se Boga ne bojiš?“

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na ozbiljnosti korizme, vjernosti Kristu i potrebi da se licemjerje ne prešućuje može biti katolički opravdan, ali tvrdnja da katolici ne smiju ići na koncerte tijekom korizme ili Velikoga tjedna nije potkrijepljena dostupnim izvorima i izrečena je kao opća zabrana. Osuda klera zbog žalovanja te nazivanje suvremenika „farizejima“ i zavodnicima bez jasno navedenih dokaza riskiraju nepravedno osuđivanje i manjak kršćanske sućuti.
concerns: Nije pružena potpora tvrdnji da katolici općenito ne smiju ići na koncerte u korizmi ili Velikom tjednu; treba razlikovati crkvene propise od osobnog pastoralnog savjeta ili prosudbe o primjerenosti pojedinog događaja.
Žalovanje za preminulom osobom samo po sebi nije znak da netko više cijeni pokojnika nego Gospodina. Izjednačavanje javno iskazane tuge s manjkom pobožnosti može biti nepravedno.
Nazvati osobe „zavodnicima“ ili pripisati im „duhovnost zavisti“ bez dokaza predstavlja ozbiljnu osudu njihovih namjera i duhovnog stanja.
Isusovi prijekori farizejima ne opravdavaju automatsko etiketiranje današnjih osoba tim nazivom; kritika treba biti istinita, razmjerna i usmjerena na konkretno ponašanje.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanska nada u uskrsnuće ne isključuje žalost: Isus je pokazao sućut ožalošćenima, a papa Franjo izričito podsjeća da Isus sam plače i da suze nisu pogrešne, premda kršćanska nada vjeruje da neće trajati zauvijek. Isusova kritika farizeja usmjerena je na licemjerje i stavljanje vanjskih obreda ispred važnijih Božjih zapovijedi, ali taj primjer poziva na istinito razlučivanje, a ne na neutemeljeno pripisivanje krivnje drugima.

citations.document_title: Eucharistic Celebration in memory of the late Supreme Pontiff Benedict XVI, and the Cardinals and Bishops deceased during the year (3 November 2023)

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on the seriousness of Lent, fidelity to Christ, and the need not to remain silent about hypocrisy can be Catholically justified, but the claim that Catholics are not allowed to go to concerts during Lent or Holy Week is not substantiated by available sources and is stated as a general prohibition. The condemnation of the clergy for mourning and calling contemporaries "Pharisees" and seducers without clearly stated evidence risk unjust condemnation and a lack of Christian compassion.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Christian hope in the resurrection does not exclude grief: Jesus showed compassion to the grieving, and Pope Francis explicitly reminds that Jesus Himself weeps and that tears are not wrong, although Christian hope trusts that they will not last forever. Jesus' criticism of the Pharisees is directed at hypocrisy and placing external rituals ahead of the more important commandments of God, but that example calls for truthful discernment, not for the unfounded imputation of guilt to others.
concerns_en: No support is provided for the claim that Catholics in general are not allowed to go to concerts in Lent or Holy Week; church regulations must be distinguished from personal pastoral advice or judgment on the appropriateness of a particular event.
Mourning for a deceased person in itself is not a sign that someone values the deceased more than the Lord. Equating publicly expressed grief with a lack of piety can be unjust.
Calling persons "seducers" or attributing to them a "spirituality of envy" without evidence represents a serious condemnation of their intentions and spiritual state.
Jesus' reproaches of the Pharisees do not automatically justify labeling people today with that title; criticism must be truthful, proportionate, and directed at specific behavior.

sections.subtitle_en: Concerts in Lent, mourning among part of the clergy, and the truth to the faces of the Pharisees
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar speaks about concerts in Lent and Holy Week and the reactions of part of the clergy
sections.content_en:
Returning to the example of the deceased singer, Grebenar admits that this situation hurt him. It concerns a beloved performer from another nation and another religion. It was emphasized about him that he "helped Catholics", while at the same time, according to the host, he held concerts throughout Catholic cities in Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina **during Lent, and even in Holy Week**, when Catholics, as he emphasizes, are not allowed to go to concerts.

Grebenar says that his "heart aches" that some from the clergy on social networks expressed greater grief for that singer than for the Lord Himself on Good Friday. Those, in his words, are the ones who post "pretty little pictures by unknown authors". He calls such people seducers who preach and host political shows, and describes their spirituality as a **"spirituality of envy"** which, according to his interpretation, is not from God.

To the question of how to relate to the Pharisees he answers: the way Jesus did, **"one must tell them the truth to their face, hypocrites"**. He ends his message with the question: "You fear the world, you fear the devil, but you do not fear the Lord. So what spirit guides you if you do not fear God?"

sections.subtitle: Evanđelje dana i dva razloga zašto Isus govori u prispodobama
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj čita evanđelje o gorušičinu zrnu i kvascu
sections.content:
Nakon psalma Grebenar čita evanđelje dana: **„Čemu je slično kraljevstvo Božje? Ono je kao kad čovjek uze gorušičino zrno i baci ga u svoj vrt. Uzraste i razvi se u stablo te mu se ptice nebeske gnijezde po granama.“** Druga prispodoba glasi: kraljevstvo je **„kao kad žena uze kvasac i zamijesi ga u tri mjere brašna dok sve ne uskisne“**.

Voditelj objašnjava da Isus i narodu i farizejima govori u prispodobama iz dva razloga. Prvi je da ih ne razumiju oni koji su „sinovi tame“, pomračenog, racionalnog i „strogo ortodoksnog“ duha. Drugi je da ih razumiju oni otvorena srca, jer im usporedba otvara oči. Takav čovjek tada kaže: „Aha, sad sam shvatio. Ovo mijenja moj odnos prema tome.“

Zato su prispodobe jednima zagonetka, a drugima **riječ spoznaje**. Grebenar ih uspoređuje s **nožem ili mačem koji reže** odnos između čovjeka i nekog pojma ili događaja. Prispodoba, kaže, ili uvelike zbuni ili prosvijetli.

magisterium.assessment: Tumačenje dobro prepoznaje da prispodobe mogu prosvijetliti one koji ih primaju otvorena srca te da kraljevstvo Božje raste iz skromnih početaka, ali podjela na „sinove tame” i otvorene slušatelje previše je pojednostavljena. Posebno je problematično povezati racionalnost ili strogu pravovjernost s duhovnom tamom: Isusove prispodobe traže svjetlo Duha i tumačenje, a katolička vjera ne suprotstavlja vjeru razumu.
concerns: Izraz „sinovi tame” u evanđeoskoj prispodobi o kukolju označava djecu Zloga, a ne ljude zato što su racionalni ili „strogo ortodoksni”; takvo poistovjećivanje nema uporište u navedenom biblijskom tekstu.

Prikaz prispodoba kao da ih razumiju samo oni koji su otvorena srca, a ne razumiju ih određeni tipovi ljudi, stvara pretjerano oštru podjelu. Isusove prispodobe bile su razumljive svakodnevnim slušateljima, ali je njihovo dublje značenje zahtijevalo objašnjenje i unutarnju rasvjetu Duha Svetoga.

Povezivanje racionalnosti s duhovnom pomračenosti može zvučati kao odbacivanje razuma. Katolički nauk, naprotiv, drži da je vjera razumna i da Božja milost prosvjetljuje razum, a ne da ga zamjenjuje ili poriče.

Izrazi „riječ spoznaje” i „nož ili mač” mogu funkcionirati kao propovjedničke slike, ali odlomak ne objašnjava njihovo značenje niti ih treba predstavljati kao izričite biblijske nazive za prispodobe.
magisterium.enrichment: Prispodobe o gorušičinu zrnu i kvascu govore o rastu kraljevstva Božjega: ono počinje skromno, ali se širi i preobražava, poput kvasca koji prožme cijelo tijesto. Isus je prispodobama povezivao otajstva kraljevstva s iskustvima iz svakodnevnog života, no učenicima je ponekad trebalo dodatno objašnjenje, a razumijevanje je povezano i s djelovanjem Duha Svetoga. Stoga je primjerenije reći da prispodoba poziva svakog slušatelja na razumijevanje i obraćenje, nego ljude unaprijed razvrstavati kao „tamne” ili otvorene; otvorenost srca i razumsko traženje istine nisu suprotnosti.

citations.document_author: The New Revised Standard Version, Catholic Edition (NRSV-CE)

magisterium.assessment_en: The interpretation rightly recognizes that parables can enlighten those who receive them with an open heart and that the kingdom of God grows from humble beginnings, but the division into “sons of darkness” and open listeners is overly simplified. It is particularly problematic to link rationality or strict orthodoxy with spiritual darkness: Jesus’ parables require the light of the Spirit and interpretation, and the Catholic faith does not oppose faith to reason.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The parables of the mustard seed and the yeast speak of the growth of the kingdom of God: it begins humbly, but spreads and transforms, like yeast that permeates the whole dough. Through parables, Jesus connected the mysteries of the kingdom with experiences from everyday life, but the disciples sometimes needed additional explanation, and understanding is also linked to the action of the Holy Spirit. Therefore, it is more appropriate to say that a parable invites every listener to understanding and conversion, rather than categorizing people in advance as “dark” or open; openness of heart and the rational search for truth are not opposites.
concerns_en: The expression “sons of darkness” in the Gospel parable of the weeds designates the children of the Evil One, and not people because they are rational or “strictly orthodox”; such an identification has no basis in the cited biblical text.

Presenting parables as though only those who are of an open heart understand them, while certain types of people do not understand them, creates an overly sharp division. Jesus’ parables were understandable to everyday listeners, but their deeper meaning required explanation and the inner illumination of the Holy Spirit.

Linking rationality with spiritual darkness can sound like a rejection of reason. Catholic teaching, on the contrary, holds that faith is reasonable and that God’s grace enlightens reason, rather than replacing or denying it.

The expressions “word of knowledge” and “knife or sword” can function as homiletic images, but the passage does not explain their meaning, nor should they be presented as explicit biblical designations for parables.

sections.subtitle_en: Gospel of the day and two reasons why Jesus speaks in parables
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host reads the Gospel about the mustard seed and the yeast
sections.content_en:
After the psalm, Grebenar reads the Gospel of the day: **“What is the kingdom of God like? It is like when a man took a mustard seed and threw it into his garden. It grew and developed into a tree, and the birds of the air nested in its branches.”** The second parable goes: the kingdom is **“like when a woman took yeast and mixed it into three measures of flour until all of it was leavened”**.

The host explains that Jesus speaks in parables to both the people and the Pharisees for two reasons. The first is so that they are not understood by those who are “sons of darkness,” of a darkened, rational, and “strictly orthodox” spirit. The second is so that they are understood by those of an open heart, because the comparison opens their eyes. Such a person then says: “Aha, now I understood. This changes my relationship toward that.”

That is why parables are a riddle to some, and to others a **word of knowledge**. Grebenar compares them to a **knife or a sword that cuts** the relationship between a person and a concept or event. A parable, he says, either greatly confuses or enlightens.

sections.subtitle: Kontrolabilnost kao grijeh lažnog katoličanstva
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar objašnjava pojam „kontrolabilnosti“ preuzet iz poslovnog svijeta
sections.content:
Kako bi opisao duh koji ne razumije prispodobe, Grebenar posuđuje pojam iz poslovnog svijeta: **kontrolabilnost**. Riječ je o katolicima koji bi kontrolirali druge, pa i samog Isusa i Duha Svetoga. Takav sustav uspoređuje s nacizmom i „najmračnijim komunizmom“, u kojima nema rasprave i ne smije se slobodno pitati.

Navodi i riječi jednog čovjeka koji mu je rekao da je **„dobio PTSP od tih kontrola“**. Grebenar to smatra razumljivim i kaže da je takvo iskustvo „gore nego da meci fijuču oko tvoje glave“. Čovjek dođe raditi na Božjoj njivi, stvoren da kroz njega govori „ričući lav, Krist Gospodin“, a dočeka ga zabrana: „Nećeš ti pričati meni o Isusu.“

Kontrolabilnost naziva **„užasom i grijehom današnjeg lažnog katoličanstva“**. Suprotstavlja joj Isusove riječi: **„Ne brani, tko nije protiv nas, za nas je.“**

magisterium.assessment: Osuda prisilne kontrole i podsjećanje na Isusovu zapovijed „Ne branite“ uglavnom su u skladu s Evanđeljem, koje učenike upozorava da ne priječe čovjeka koji djeluje u Isusovo ime. Ipak, odlomak tu izreku primjenjuje široko, a usporedbe s nacizmom, komunizmom i PTSP-om te izraz „ričući lav, Krist Gospodin“ nose rizik pretjerivanja ili teološke nejasnoće.
concerns: „Ne brani“ (Mk 9,38–40; Lk 9,49–50) nije opće odobrenje svakog djelovanja izvan crkvenog zajedništva niti znači da nema mjesta razlučivanju. Augustin uz Isusovu zabranu sprječavanja onoga što se čini u njegovo ime istodobno razlikuje dobro koje treba priznati od raskola i pogrešaka koje treba ispravljati.

Usporedba kontrole u crkvenoj zajednici s nacizmom i „najmračnijim komunizmom“ može biti retorička analogija, ali bez dodatnog objašnjenja može neprimjereno izjednačiti različite vrste zla i iskustava.

Tvrdnju da je takvo iskustvo „gore nego da meci fijuču oko tvoje glave“ ne treba shvatiti kao teološki zaključak niti kao procjenu tuđe traume; usporedba može umanjiti ozbiljnost ratnog iskustva i psihičke patnje.

Izraz „ričući lav, Krist Gospodin“ može zbuniti: u 1 Pt 5,8 slika ričućeg lava označava đavla, a ne Krista. Ako je riječ o pjesničkoj aluziji na Kristovu pobjedu ili „Lava iz Judina plemena“ (Otk 5,5), trebalo bi to jasno razlikovati.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusova zapovijed „Ne branite“ u kontekstu se odnosi na čovjeka koji u Isusovo ime čini dobro, iako ne pripada skupini učenika; ona ispravlja njihovu zatvorenost, ali ne ukida potrebu za crkvenim zajedništvom i razlučivanjem. Augustin objašnjava da treba priznati ono što je istinito i dobro, a odbacivati ono što razara jedinstvo i proturječi istini.

citations.document_title: De baptismo contra Donatistas, liber I

magisterium.assessment_en: The condemnation of coercive control and the reminder of Jesus' command "Do not forbid" are largely in accordance with the Gospel, which warns the disciples not to hinder a man who acts in Jesus' name. However, the passage applies that saying broadly, and the comparisons with Nazism, communism, and PTSD, as well as the phrase "roaring lion, Christ the Lord", carry a risk of exaggeration or theological ambiguity.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' command "Do not forbid" in context refers to a man who does good in Jesus' name, even though he does not belong to the group of disciples; it corrects their closedness, but does not abolish the need for ecclesial communion and discernment. Augustine explains that one should recognize what is true and good, and reject what destroys unity and contradicts the truth.
concerns_en: "Do not forbid" (Mk 9:38–40; Lk 9:49–50) is not a general approval of every action outside ecclesial communion, nor does it mean there is no place for discernment. Alongside Jesus' prohibition against hindering what is done in his name, Augustine simultaneously distinguishes the good that should be recognized from schism and errors that should be corrected.

The comparison of control within an ecclesial community to Nazism and the "darkest communism" may be a rhetorical analogy, but without further explanation it can inappropriately equate different kinds of evil and experiences.

The claim that such an experience is "worse than bullets whizzing around your head" should not be taken as a theological conclusion nor as an assessment of someone else's trauma; the comparison may diminish the seriousness of war experience and psychological suffering.

The expression "roaring lion, Christ the Lord" can be confusing: in 1 Pet 5:8 the image of a roaring lion signifies the devil, not Christ. If it is a poetic allusion to Christ's victory or the "Lion of the tribe of Judah" (Rev 5:5), this should be clearly distinguished.

sections.subtitle_en: Controllability as a Sin of False Catholicism
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar explains the concept of "controllability" borrowed from the business world
sections.content_en:
In order to describe a spirit that does not understand parables, Grebenar borrows a concept from the business world: **controllability**. This refers to Catholics who would control others, even Jesus himself and the Holy Spirit. He compares such a system to Nazism and the "darkest communism", in which there is no discussion and one is not allowed to freely ask questions.

He also cites the words of a man who told him that he **"got PTSD from those controls"**. Grebenar considers this understandable and says that such an experience is "worse than bullets whizzing around your head". A person comes to work in God's field, created so that through him speaks the "roaring lion, Christ the Lord", only to be met with a prohibition: "You will not speak to me about Jesus."

He calls controllability the **"horror and sin of today's false Catholicism"**. He counters it with Jesus' words: **"Do not forbid, for whoever is not against us is for us."**

sections.subtitle: Pravi brat pomaže, lažni vreba, a jedini branitelj bio je razbojnik
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pripovijeda o dobrom razbojniku koji je jedini obranio Isusa na križu
sections.content:
Grebenar suprotstavlja dva duha. **Farizejski duh** sluša, ali je zbunjen i ne razumije. **Apostolski duh**, duh svetaca, otvoren je za Božju riječ, post, molitvu, evangelizaciju i obraćenja. Raduje se kad čuje da se nekome promijenio život.

Odatle izvodi sliku **pravog brata**. Kad brat ili sestra koji su uspješni u evangelizaciji padnu ili pogriješe, pravi brat moli za njih, priskače im u pomoć i ohrabruje ih. Opominje ih dobronamjerno, a onaj tko primi opomenu zahvaljuje Bogu što su mu se „otvorile oči“. **Lažni brat**, nasuprot tome, čeka i vreba, kao što su farizeji vrebali Isusa na riječi. Osudili su ga unaprijed jer je prokazivao tamu, pakost i zavist njihovih srca. Takva su srca, kaže voditelj, toliko podmukla da „možeš umirati pored njega, neće ti ruku pružiti“.

Na vrhuncu te slike nalazi se Kalvarija. Prema jednom od evanđelja, kako navodi Grebenar, oba su se razbojnika najprije rugala Isusu. No kad je jedan vidio količinu mržnje i prezira prema Isusu, obratio se. Taj „dobri razbojnik“, naglašava voditelj, nije bio dobar, i sam je priznao: „Mi smo ovdje zaslužili da visimo na križu, ali Isus nije.“ **Od svih prisutnih, uključujući farizeje koji su poučavali narod o vjeri, Isusa je obranio samo razbojnik.** Zato, zaključuje Grebenar, Isus farizejima kaže: „Pretekoše vas bludnice i carinici u kraljevstvo Božje.“

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na bratsku pomoć, dobronamjernu opomenu i radost zbog obraćenja u skladu je s kršćanskim naukom o brizi za duhovno dobro bližnjega. Ipak, prikaz farizeja kao jedinstvene skupine zlonamjernika te pojedinosti o razbojnicima i „jedinom branitelju“ Isusa zahtijevaju biblijsku nijansu i preciziranje.
concerns: Evangelizacija, molitva, post i dobronamjerna bratska opomena prikazani su pozitivno, ali oznaka „farizejski duh“ ne bi se smjela poistovjetiti sa svim farizejima ili svakim vjernikom koji ne razumije neku poruku; evanđeoska kritika usmjerena je na konkretno licemjerje i tvrdoću srca.

Tvrdnja da su se oba razbojnika najprije rugala Isusu, a zatim se jedan obratio nakon što je vidio mržnju prema njemu, nije izričito ispričana u Lukinu evanđelju: Luka prikazuje jednog koji vrijeđa Isusa i drugoga koji ga kori, priznaje vlastitu krivnju i moli Isusa da ga se sjeti. Važno je razlikovati tekst evanđelja od naknadne pretpostavke o tome kako se obraćenje dogodilo.

Tvrdnja da je razbojnik bio jedini koji je branio Isusa pretjerana je kao sažetak evanđeoskih izvještaja: u Lk 23,47 stotnik također slavi Boga i proglašava Isusa pravednim. Također, izjava „pretekoše vas bludnice i carinici“ govori o prednosti onih koji se kaju i vrše Očevu volju, a ne o tome da je svaka osoba koja pripada vjerskom vodstvu nužno zatvorena obraćenju.
magisterium.enrichment: Dobri razbojnik nije prikazan kao čovjek koji je oduvijek bio dobar, nego kao krivac koji se u posljednjem času iskreno kaje, priznaje Isusovu nevinost i pouzdaje se u njegovo milosrđe; crkveno razmatranje tog prizora naglašava da s Kristom nije prekasno vratiti se Bogu. Bratska opomena stoga treba služiti spasenju drugoga, a ne ponižavanju ili osudi: crkveno učenje povezuje brigu za bližnjega s pažnjom prema njegovu duhovnom dobru.
magisterium.assessment_en: The call to fraternal help, well-intentioned admonition, and joy over conversion is in accordance with Christian teaching on care for the spiritual good of one's neighbor. Nevertheless, the portrayal of the Pharisees as a uniform group of ill-intentioned people and the details about the robbers and the "only defender" of Jesus require biblical nuance and precision.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The good thief is not portrayed as a man who was always good, but as a guilty person who at the last moment sincerely repents, acknowledges Jesus' innocence, and trusts in his mercy; the Church's reflection on that scene emphasizes that with Christ it is not too late to return to God. Fraternal correction should therefore serve the salvation of the other, not humiliation or condemnation: Church teaching connects care for one's neighbor with attentiveness toward his spiritual good.
concerns_en: Evangelization, prayer, fasting, and well-intentioned fraternal correction are presented positively, but the label "Pharisaic spirit" should not be equated with all Pharisees or every believer who does not understand a message; evangelical criticism is directed at concrete hypocrisy and hardness of heart.

The claim that both robbers initially mocked Jesus, and then one converted after seeing the hatred toward him, is not explicitly recounted in Luke's Gospel: Luke depicts one who reviles Jesus and the other who rebukes him, acknowledges his own guilt, and asks Jesus to remember him. It is important to distinguish the Gospel text from a subsequent assumption about how the conversion occurred.

The claim that the robber was the only one who defended Jesus is exaggerated as a summary of the Gospel accounts: in Lk 23:47 the centurion also praises God and declares Jesus innocent. Also, the statement "prostitutes and tax collectors precede you" speaks of the precedence of those who repent and do the Father's will, not that every person belonging to the religious leadership is necessarily closed to conversion.

sections.subtitle_en: A true brother helps, a false one lies in wait, and the only defender was a robber
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host narrates about the good thief who was the only one to defend Jesus on the cross
sections.content_en:
Grebenar contrasts two spirits. **The Pharisaic spirit** listens, but is confused and does not understand. **The apostolic spirit**, the spirit of the saints, is open to God's word, fasting, prayer, evangelization, and conversions. It rejoices when it hears that someone's life has changed.

From this he derives the image of a **true brother**. When a brother or sister who are successful in evangelization fall or make a mistake, a true brother prays for them, rushes to their aid, and encourages them. He admonishes them with good intentions, and the one who receives the admonition thanks God that his "eyes were opened". **A false brother**, by contrast, waits and lies in wait, just as the Pharisees lay in wait for Jesus in his words. They condemned him in advance because he exposed the darkness, malice, and envy of their hearts. Such hearts, says the host, are so insidious that "you could be dying next to him, he will not extend a hand to you".

At the peak of this image is Calvary. According to one of the Gospels, as Grebenar states, both robbers initially mocked Jesus. But when one saw the amount of hatred and contempt toward Jesus, he converted. That "good thief", emphasizes the host, was not good, and he himself admitted: "We deserved to hang on the cross here, but Jesus did not." **Of all those present, including the Pharisees who taught the people about faith, only the robber defended Jesus.** Therefore, concludes Grebenar, Jesus says to the Pharisees: "Prostitutes and tax collectors precede you into the kingdom of God."

sections.subtitle: Egzorcizam nad samim sobom: tjerati farizeja iz vlastitog srca
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar govori o vođenju velike inicijative bez duha kontrole
sections.content:
Tko se boji Boga, ističe Grebenar, tražit će farizeja u sebi. Takvi ljudi **„rade egzorcizam sami nad sobom“**. Iz sebe tjeraju farizejsku vjeru razuma, kontrolu nad drugima i uvjerenje da sve ovisi o njima i da se njih mora sve pitati, „kao Bog“.

Voditelj to povezuje s vlastitim iskustvom vodstva. Bio je direktor u velikoj tvrtki, a danas vodi veliku domoljubnu inicijativu s mnogo ljudi. Kaže da ne želi takav duh. Priznaje da se o važnim i velikim odlukama mora pitati i da on za neke stvari mora znati. No kad mu netko s osmijehom dođe i kaže da je u molitvi dobio poticaj nešto pokrenuti, moliti ili postiti, to se, prema njegovim riječima, ne smije spriječiti. Tada srce gori: „Vidi kako je Bog zahvatio njegovo srce. Bože, proslavi se.“

Za svakoga nudi i test: **„Da li se ja Boga bojim?“** Tko se boji da mu Bog ne kaže „bezakoniče“, zaključuje, na dobrom je putu i otjerao je od sebe duh farizejštine.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s evanđeoskim pozivom na obraćenje srca, poniznost i odustajanje od licemjerja, samopravednosti i nepravedne kontrole drugih. Ipak, neke formulacije traže pojašnjenje: razum nije sam po sebi farizejski, a osobni poticaj u molitvi treba razborito razlučivati, dok strah Božji nije samo bojazan od osude.
concerns: Izraz „farizejska vjera razuma” može zvučati kao da je razum protiv vjere; katolička kritika farizejštine odnosi se na licemjerje, samopravednost i zanemarivanje važnijih Božjih zapovijedi, a ne na razumno promišljanje kao takvo.

Poticaj koji netko pripisuje molitvi ne treba automatski slijediti niti ga voditelj uvijek mora pustiti da se ostvari: valja ga razlučivati prema vjeri i dobru zajednice te uvažavati odgovornu službu vodstva.
„Egzorcizam sami nad sobom” može biti razumljiva metafora za osobno obraćenje, ali nije doslovni egzorcizam; bilo bi dobro izbjeći dojam da pojedinac sam nad sobom obavlja crkveni obred.

Mjerilo da se čovjek boji da mu Bog ne kaže „bezakoniče” može prenaglasiti strah od osude; strah Božji u kršćanskom životu uključuje poštovanje i svijest o odgovornosti pred Bogom, ali vodi i pouzdanju u njegovo milosrđe.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusova kritika farizeja usmjerena je na raskorak između izvanjskog vjerskog ponašanja i unutarnje pravednosti, a ne na vjeru, molitvu ili razum same po sebi; Katekizam također napominje da Kristovi odnosi s farizejima nisu bili isključivo polemički. Zato je zdravo ispitivanje vlastitih motiva povezano s poniznošću i obraćenjem, ali ne bi smjelo postati osuđivanje drugih ni skrupulozan strah.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with the evangelical call to conversion of heart, humility, and the renunciation of hypocrisy, self-righteousness, and unjust control of others. However, some formulations require clarification: reason is not in itself Pharisaic, and a personal impulse in prayer should be prudently discerned, while the fear of God is not merely fear of condemnation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' criticism of the Pharisees is directed at the discrepancy between external religious behavior and internal righteousness, not at faith, prayer, or reason in themselves; the Catechism also notes that Christ's relations with the Pharisees were not exclusively polemical. Therefore, a healthy examination of one's own motives is connected with humility and conversion, but it should not become condemnation of others nor scrupulous fear.
concerns_en: The expression "Pharisaic faith of reason" can sound as though reason is contrary to faith; Catholic criticism of Pharisaism pertains to hypocrisy, self-righteousness, and the neglect of the weightier commandments of God, not to rational reflection as such.

An impulse that someone attributes to prayer should not be automatically followed, nor must a leader always allow it to be realized: it should be discerned according to faith and the good of the community, while respecting the responsible office of leadership.

"Exorcism on oneself" can be an understandable metaphor for personal conversion, but it is not a literal exorcism; it would be good to avoid the impression that an individual performs an ecclesiastical rite upon oneself.

The criterion that a person fears that God might say to him "worker of lawlessness" can overemphasize the fear of condemnation; the fear of God in Christian life includes reverence and an awareness of responsibility before God, but it also leads to trust in his mercy.

sections.subtitle_en: Exorcism over oneself: driving the Pharisee out of one's own heart
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar speaks about leading a large initiative without a spirit of control
sections.content_en:
Whoever fears God, Grebenar emphasizes, will seek the Pharisee within himself. Such people **"perform an exorcism on themselves"**. They drive out of themselves the Pharisaic faith of reason, control over others, and the conviction that everything depends on them and that they must be consulted on everything, "like God".

The leader connects this with his own experience of leadership. He was a director in a large company, and today he leads a large patriotic initiative with many people. He says that he does not want such a spirit. He admits that he must be consulted about important and big decisions and that there are certain things he must know about. But when someone comes to him with a smile and says that in prayer they received an impulse to initiate something, to pray or to fast, that, according to his words, must not be prevented. Then the heart burns: "Look how God has captured his heart. God, be glorified."

For everyone, he also offers a test: **"Do I fear God?"** Whoever fears that God might say to him "worker of lawlessness", he concludes, is on the right path and has driven the spirit of Pharisaism away from himself.

sections.subtitle: Gorušičino zrno i kvasac: Bog djeluje kroz neznatno, skriveno i strpljivo
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj tumači sliku gorušičina zrna koje nitko ne vidi
sections.content:
Grebenar potom tumači same prispodobe. Gorušičino je zrno toliko sitno i neznatno da ga nitko ne vidi, a ako padne, ne može se naći. Bog, objašnjava voditelj, djeluje upravo kroz ono što u ljudskim očima nema vrijednost. Podsjeća na pitanje: **„Iz Nazareta, može li što dobro izaći?“** Bog daje znakove i potvrde, ali ne nužno spektakularne. Oni se razlučuju i spoznaju duhom i srcem. Otvorenima se otkrivaju, a drugima ne znače ništa.

Zrno raste skriveno od očiju svijeta i treba mu vremena. Nitko ne zna što je dok ne proklija i ne pusti lišće. Tada izraste u stablo u kojem se ptice gnijezde. Ptice su, prema Grebenarovu tumačenju, **slika anđela i svetih koji dolaze služiti**.

Druga prispodoba, o kvascu, govori o vremenu. Žena zamijesi tijesto i ostavi ga preko noći. Na njemu ne radi, nego „Bog radi s njim nešto“. **„Za nešto veliko, vrijedno, važno, ukusno, pravo mora proći vrijeme“**, naglašava voditelj. Primjer je sam Isus, koji je **30 godina u skrovitosti radio s Josipom u radionici**. Ni susjedi nisu znali da je Mesija dok nije došlo vrijeme i dok nije rekao da se ostvarilo Pismo. Čak je i apostolima zaprijetio da to ne govore dok ne dođe trenutak. Pitanje „Jesi li ti Mesija?“, primjećuje Grebenar, dugo je ostalo otvoreno.

magisterium.assessment: Središnja poruka — da Kraljevstvo Božje raste iz skromnih početaka, djelovanjem koje je često skriveno i postupno — dobro je utemeljena u Isusovim prispodobama i katoličkom tumačenju njihova značenja. Ipak, nekoliko detalja izneseno je kao sigurno tumačenje ili činjenica premda ih evanđeoski tekstovi ne potvrđuju izravno, pa bi ih trebalo izraziti opreznije.
concerns: Tvrdnja da su ptice u granama slika anđela i svetih nije objašnjenje koje se može utvrditi iz priloženog evanđeoskog teksta; prikladnije je predstaviti je kao moguću simboličku interpretaciju, a ne kao utvrđeno značenje.

U prispodobi o kvascu Isus kaže da kvasac prožima tijesto, ali ne navodi da ga žena ostavlja preko noći niti izrijekom kaže da je poanta u tome da čovjek prestaje raditi dok Bog djeluje. To može poslužiti kao duhovna primjena, no treba je razlikovati od samog teksta i paziti da ne zanemari ljudsku suradnju, koju nauk o rastu Kraljevstva također ističe.

Evanđelja ne pripovijedaju da je Isus svih trideset godina radio s Josipom u radionici; govore o Isusovu skrivenom životu u Nazaretu, a crkveno tumačenje podupire da ga je Josip poučavao zanatu. Stoga je sigurnije reći da je Isus živio i radio u obiteljskom i nazaretskom okruženju, bez tvrdnje da je poznat svaki detalj svih tih godina.

Tvrdnja da susjedi nisu znali da je Isus Mesija te da je pitanje njegove mesijanske uloge dugo ostalo otvoreno široka je povijesna generalizacija koju priloženi tekstovi ne potvrđuju. Evanđelja prikazuju različite reakcije na Isusov identitet i njegovu službu; tvrdnje o tome što su susjedi znali ili kada su razumjeli trebaju biti jasno označene kao zaključak, a ne izravni biblijski podatak.
magisterium.enrichment: Prispodobe o gorušičinu zrnu i kvascu prikazuju dva povezana vida rasta Kraljevstva: širenje iz malenih početaka te preobrazbu koja zahvaća čitavu stvarnost. Crkveno tumačenje naglašava da je taj rast plod Božjeg djelovanja, ali i da ljudska raspoloživost i slobodna suradnja utječu na njegovo prihvaćanje. Isusov skroviti život u Nazaretu svjedoči da običan obiteljski život i rad nisu izgubljeno vrijeme, nego dio njegova poslanja i put posvećenja svakodnevice.

magisterium.assessment_en: The central message—that the Kingdom of God grows from humble beginnings, through an action that is often hidden and gradual—is well founded in Jesus' parables and Catholic interpretation of their meaning. However, several details are presented as certain interpretation or fact even though the Gospel texts do not confirm them directly, so they should be expressed more cautiously.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The parables of the mustard seed and the yeast present two related aspects of the growth of the Kingdom: expansion from small beginnings and the transformation that encompasses all reality. Church teaching emphasizes that this growth is the fruit of God's action, but also that human readiness and free cooperation affect its reception. Jesus' hidden life in Nazareth testifies that ordinary family life and work are not lost time, but part of His mission and a path of sanctification of everyday life.
concerns_en: The assertion that the birds in the branches are an image of angels and saints is not an explanation that can be established from the attached Gospel text; it is more appropriate to present it as a possible symbolic interpretation, rather than an established meaning.

In the parable of the yeast, Jesus says that the yeast permeates the dough, but He does not state that the woman leaves it overnight, nor does He explicitly say that the point is that man ceases to work while God acts. This can serve as a spiritual application, but it should be distinguished from the text itself, and care should be taken not to neglect human cooperation, which the teaching on the growth of the Kingdom also emphasizes.

The Gospels do not recount that Jesus worked with Joseph in the workshop for all thirty years; they speak of Jesus' hidden life in Nazareth, and Church interpretation supports that Joseph taught Him the trade. Therefore, it is safer to say that Jesus lived and worked in the family and Nazareth environment, without claiming that every detail of all those years is known.

The assertion that the neighbors did not know that Jesus was the Messiah and that the question of His messianic role remained open for a long time is a broad historical generalization not confirmed by the attached texts. The Gospels show varied reactions to Jesus' identity and His ministry; claims about what the neighbors knew or when they understood should be clearly designated as an inference, not direct biblical data.

sections.subtitle_en: The Mustard Seed and the Yeast: God Acts Through the Insignificant, Hidden, and Patient
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host interprets the image of the mustard seed that no one sees
sections.content_en:
Grebenar then interprets the parables themselves. The mustard seed is so tiny and insignificant that no one sees it, and if it falls, it cannot be found. God, the host explains, acts precisely through what has no value in human eyes. He recalls the question: **„From Nazareth, can anything good come?“** God gives signs and confirmations, but not necessarily spectacular ones. They are discerned and known by the spirit and the heart. They are revealed to the open, while to others they mean nothing.

The seed grows hidden from the eyes of the world and needs time. No one knows what it is until it sprouts and puts forth leaves. Then it grows into a tree in which birds nest. Birds are, according to Grebenar's interpretation, **an image of angels and saints who come to serve**.

The second parable, about the yeast, speaks of time. A woman kneads dough and leaves it overnight. She does not work on it, but rather „God is doing something with it“. **„For something great, valuable, important, tasty, genuine, time must pass“**, the host emphasizes. An example is Jesus Himself, who **for 30 years in hiddenness worked with Joseph in the workshop**. Even the neighbors did not know that He was the Messiah until the time came and until He said that the Scripture was fulfilled. He even strictly ordered the apostles not to say this until the moment came. The question „Are you the Messiah?“, Grebenar notes, remained open for a long time.

Sama najava domoljubne inicijative i raspored promocija ne sadržavaju dovoljno teološkog sadržaja za višu ocjenu.
concerns: Podnaslov o sprječavanju demonskih utjecaja mogao bi potaknuti pretjerano pripisivanje teškoća djelovanju demona, ali odlomak ne tvrdi da su pojedini problemi demonskog podrijetla niti objašnjava metodu knjige; Crkva upozorava na oprez u prosuđivanju takvih pojava.
magisterium.enrichment: Krunica je katolička marijanska pobožnost koja može podupirati molitvu i nutarnju borbu, ali njezino moljenje treba biti usmjereno na sabrano razmatranje otajstava, a ne na puko mehaničko izgovaranje riječi. Katolički nauk priznaje djelovanje đavla i demona, ali također naglašava ljudsku slobodu, granice njihova djelovanja i potrebu opreza pri tumačenju konkretnih događaja.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic practice because it announces the prayer of the Rosary and does not make claims that would contradict teaching or Sacred Scripture; however, the content of the book and the way it treats demonic influences are not presented here and thus cannot be theologically evaluated. The announcement itself of the patriotic initiative and the promotion schedule do not contain sufficient theological content for a higher rating.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Rosary is a Catholic Marian devotion that can support prayer and internal struggle, but its recitation should be directed toward focused contemplation of the mysteries, rather than mere mechanical uttering of words. Catholic teaching recognizes the activity of the devil and demons, but it also emphasizes human freedom, the limits of their activity, and the need for caution when interpreting concrete events.
concerns_en: The subtitle on preventing demonic influences could encourage an excessive attribution of difficulties to the work of demons, but the passage does not claim that specific problems are of demonic origin nor does it explain the book's method; the Church advises caution in discerning such phenomena.

sections.subtitle: Članstvo u Ora et labora: strpljivost i bez obvezne članarine
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj poziva na učlanjenje u inicijativu i naglašava da je članstvo besplatno
sections.content:
Grebenar poziva gledatelje da postanu članovi **domoljubne inicijative Ora et labora**. Pritom traži strpljivost i povezuje je s upravo protumačenim evanđeljem: zrno mora rasti, tijesto se mora dići, a „ne ide to za tri minute“. Sve što je vrijedno za kraljevstvo Božje, kaže, traži vremena, kao što ga traži podizanje obitelji ili stjecanje zvanja.

Za one s otvorenim pitanjima na ekranu su istaknuti brojevi mobitela za Hrvatsku i za Bosnu i Hercegovinu. Voditelj ističe da je podrška inicijativi **potpuno dobrovoljna**. Član se može postati **bez članarine i bez donacije**. „Ne znam gdje još ima da možeš biti član, a ne moraš ništa dati“, kaže. Kritičare koje naziva farizejima, a koji tvrde da on ljudima naplaćuje članarine, otpravlja riječima: „Jad i beda.“

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na strpljivost, oslonjen na prispodobe o gorušičinu zrnu i kvascu, u osnovi je u skladu s evanđeoskom poukom da Kraljevstvo Božje raste postupno i često neprimjetno. Ipak, nazivanje kritičara „farizejima” i odbacivanje njihova prigovora izrazom „jad i beda” mogu biti nespojivi s duhom strpljivosti i dijaloga koji se u odlomku inače zagovara, a bilo bi važno ne poistovjetiti rast određene inicijative s rastom Kraljevstva Božjega.
concerns: Prispodobe o sjemenu i kvascu govore o rastu Kraljevstva Božjega; njihova primjena na organizaciju može biti prikladna kao analogija, ali ne bi smjela sugerirati da su uspjeh ili članstvo u konkretnoj inicijativi sami po sebi mjerilo duhovnog rasta.

Označavanje kritičara „farizejima” može djelovati kao omalovažavanje, a ne kao odgovor na njihove konkretne primjedbe. Papinsko tumačenje evanđeoske strpljivosti naglašava da se slabosti i pogreške susreću s poštovanjem i blagošću, ne s prezirom.
magisterium.enrichment: Prispodoba o sjemenu naglašava da rast Kraljevstva ovisi o Božjem djelovanju, ali i o ljudskom prihvaćanju i odgovornom odgovoru; zato strpljivost ne znači pasivnost niti jamči da je svaka inicijativa Božje djelo. Dobrovoljno članstvo bez članarine ili donacije, kako je opisano u odlomku, samo po sebi ne predstavlja teološki problem; ipak, kritike je primjerenije razjasniti mirno i činjenično, čuvajući dostojanstvo osoba i otvorenost za dijalog.
magisterium.assessment_en: The call for patience, grounded in the parables of the mustard seed and the leaven, is essentially in accordance with the evangelical teaching that the Kingdom of God grows gradually and often imperceptibly. Nevertheless, calling critics "Pharisees" and dismissing their objection with the expression "misery and wretchedness" may be incompatible with the spirit of patience and dialogue that is otherwise advocated in the passage, and it would be important not to equate the growth of a particular initiative with the growth of the Kingdom of God.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The parable of the seed emphasizes that the growth of the Kingdom depends on God's action, but also on human acceptance and a responsible response; therefore, patience does not mean passivity, nor does it guarantee that every initiative is God's work. Voluntary membership without a membership fee or donation, as described in the passage, does not in itself present a theological problem; nevertheless, it is more appropriate to clarify criticisms calmly and factually, preserving the dignity of persons and openness to dialogue.
concerns_en: The parables of the seed and the leaven speak of the growth of the Kingdom of God; their application to an organization may be appropriate as an analogy, but it should not suggest that success or membership in a concrete initiative are in themselves a measure of spiritual growth.

Labeling critics as "Pharisees" may come across as belittling rather than as a response to their specific objections. The papal interpretation of evangelical patience emphasizes that weaknesses and mistakes are met with respect and gentleness, not with contempt.

sections.subtitle_en: Membership in Ora et labora: patience and no mandatory membership fee
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host invites viewers to join the initiative and emphasizes that membership is free
sections.content_en:
Grebenar invites viewers to become members of the **patriotic initiative Ora et labora**. In doing so, he asks for patience and connects it with the Gospel that was just interpreted: the grain must grow, the dough must rise, and "it doesn't happen in three minutes." Everything that is worthwhile for the kingdom of God, he says, takes time, just as raising a family or acquiring a profession takes it.

For those with open questions, mobile phone numbers for Hrvatska and for Bosna i Hercegovina are highlighted on the screen. The host emphasizes that support for the initiative is **completely voluntary**. One can become a member **without a membership fee and without a donation**. "I don't know where else it exists that you can be a member and don't have to give anything," he says. Critics whom he calls Pharisees, and who claim that he charges people membership fees, he dismisses with the words: "Misery and wretchedness."

sections.subtitle: Svjedočanstva o ozdravljenjima: rijetka bolest i nalazi bolji za 50 posto
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar čita svjedočanstva vjernica o ozdravljenjima
sections.content:
Pri kraju emisije Grebenar čita svjedočanstva gledateljica. **Božana** piše da je njezin muž ozdravio od autoimune bolesti. Bolest je bila toliko rijetka da je, prema njezinim riječima, u cijeloj Njemačkoj imalo oko 800 oboljelih. „Nisam ni sumnjala jer toliko čuda Božjih sam doživjela. Isus moj, sve moje, moj početak, moj kraj“, poručuje. Voditelj objašnjava da Isus daje takve znakove kako bi čovjek spoznao da je Bog s njim i u njemu.

**Tereza** svjedoči o sestri koja je, unatoč karcinomu dojke, postila pet dana. Govorili su joj da to nije za nju, a ona je odgovorila: **„Ja sam pozvana i odazivam se.“** Nakana joj je bila zdravlje sina, kojemu su loše vrijednosti na bubrezima i prijeti mu odstranjivanje bubrega. Tijekom posta osjećala je više snage i energije. Sin joj je potom javio da su mu **sve vrijednosti u krvi i urinu pale za više od 50 posto**. „Suze radosnice su potekle“, piše Tereza, i zahvaljuje Bogu, Isusu, Mariji, Duhu Svetom i svetom Josipu.

Grebenar zahvaljuje na svjedočanstvima i podsjeća na još jednu Isusovu posljednju riječ: **„Bit ćete mi svjedoci do na kraj svijeta.“** Dodaje da se, Božjom milošću, zajedničkim molitvama i postovima, ovaj podcast čuje „do na kraj svijeta“.

magisterium.assessment: Molitva za ozdravljenje, zahvalnost i svjedočenje o Božjem djelovanju u skladu su s katoličkim naukom: Isusova ozdravljenja znak su blizine Kraljevstva, a Crkva moli za bolesne i skrbi za njih. Ipak, odlomak treba jasnije razlikovati osobno svjedočanstvo od medicinski potvrđenog čuda te izbjeći da petodnevni post osobe oboljele od raka zvuči kao postupak koji bi drugi trebali oponašati.
concerns: Podatak da su nalazi pali za više od 50 posto jest svjedočanstvo o promjeni nalaza, ali sam po sebi ne utvrđuje ni njezin medicinski uzrok ni trajnost poboljšanja; ne bi ga trebalo predstavljati kao dokaz čudesnog ozdravljenja bez stručne procjene.

Petodnevni post osobe s karcinomom dojke može biti zdravstveno rizičan. Budući da je u svjedočanstvu istaknuto da je postila unatoč upozorenjima da to nije za nju, valja izričito pojasniti da post nije zamjena za liječenje te da se u bolesti mora razborito uskladiti sa zdravstvenim stanjem i liječničkim savjetom.

Tvrdnja da Isus daje ozdravljenja kako bi čovjek spoznao da je Bog s njim može biti prihvatljiva ako se razumije kao govor o znaku i osobnom svjedočanstvu, a ne kao opće obećanje da će vjera ili post dovesti do fizičkog ozdravljenja. Katolički nauk izričito napominje da Isus nije ozdravio sve bolesne i da ni najintenzivnija molitva ne postiže uvijek ozdravljenje.

Završna rečenica pripisuje Isusu riječi Bit ćete mi svjedoci do na kraj svijeta; čini se da je riječ o slobodnoj parafrazi, a ne preciznom navodu. Radi jasnoće bolje ju je označiti kao parafrazu Dj 1,8 ili navesti biblijski tekst točno.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička tradicija potiče molitvu za ozdravljenje i prepoznaje da tjelesna ozdravljenja mogu biti znakom Kristove blizine i njegova kraljevstva, ali ne svodi Božje djelovanje na vidljiv oporavak: bolestan čovjek može svjedočiti Kristu i kroz vjeru, strpljivost i nadu usred bolesti. Crkva zato spaja molitvu s konkretnom skrbi i liječenjem, a bolesnima osobito pruža sakrament bolesničkog pomazanja.

citations.document_author: Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith

magisterium.assessment_en: Prayer for healing, gratitude, and testifying to God's action are in accordance with Catholic teaching: Jesus' healings are a sign of the closeness of the Kingdom, and the Church prays for the sick and cares for them. Nevertheless, the passage should more clearly distinguish personal testimony from a medically confirmed miracle and avoid having the five-day fast of a person suffering from cancer sound like an action that others should imitate.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic tradition encourages prayer for healing and recognizes that physical healings can be a sign of Christ's closeness and his kingdom, but it does not reduce God's action to visible recovery: a sick person can witness to Christ also through faith, patience, and hope in the midst of illness. The Church therefore unites prayer with concrete care and medical treatment, and especially offers the sick the sacrament of the anointing of the sick.
concerns_en: The information that the test results dropped by more than 50 percent is a testimony about a change in results, but in itself it establishes neither its medical cause nor the permanence of the improvement; it should not be presented as proof of a miraculous healing without professional evaluation.

A five-day fast of a person with breast cancer can pose a health risk. Since the testimony emphasizes that she fasted despite warnings that this was not for her, it should be explicitly clarified that fasting is not a substitute for medical treatment and that in illness it must be prudently aligned with one's state of health and medical advice.

The claim that Jesus gives healings so that man may know that God is with him can be acceptable if understood as speaking of a sign and personal testimony, and not as a general promise that faith or fasting will lead to physical healing. Catholic teaching explicitly notes that Jesus did not heal all the sick and that even the most intense prayer does not always achieve healing.

The concluding sentence attributes to Jesus the words „You will be my witnesses to the end of the earth“; it seems to be a loose paraphrase rather than a precise quotation. For the sake of clarity, it is better to designate it as a paraphrase of Acts 1:8 or to cite the biblical text accurately.

sections.subtitle_en: Testimonies of healings: a rare disease and test results better by 50 percent
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar reads testimonies of female believers about healings
sections.content_en:
Near the end of the show, Grebenar reads testimonies of female viewers. **Božana** writes that her husband was healed of an autoimmune disease. The disease was so rare that, according to her words, about 800 sufferers had it in all of Germany. „I did not even doubt because I experienced so many of God's miracles. My Jesus, my all, my beginning, my end,“ she conveys. The host explains that Jesus gives such signs so that man may come to know that God is with him and in him.

**Tereza** testifies about a sister who, despite breast cancer, fasted for five days. They were telling her that this was not for her, and she answered: **„I am called and I respond.“** Her intention was the health of her son, whose kidney values are bad and who is threatened with kidney removal. During the fast, she felt more strength and energy. Her son then informed her that **all his values in blood and urine dropped by more than 50 percent**. „Tears of joy flowed,“ Tereza writes, and gives thanks to God, Jesus, Mary, the Holy Spirit, and Saint Joseph.

Grebenar expresses thanks for the testimonies and recalls another final word of Jesus: **„You will be my witnesses to the end of the earth.“** He adds that, by God's grace, through mutual prayers and fasts, this podcast is heard „to the end of the earth“.

sections.subtitle: Poziv muškarcima na trgove, blagoslov i centar Kraljica Mira u Međugorju
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj poziva muškarce na javnu molitvu krunice na trgovima
sections.content:
Grebenar upućuje poziv **muškarcima iz Njemačke i Austrije** na javnu molitvu krunice **u Zagrebu 7. studenoga**. Muškarce u Hrvatskoj i Bosni i Hercegovini poziva da pokrenu molitvu krunice na trgu u svom gradu ili općini. Ako im to ne dopuste, neka mole kraj crkve ili, kako duhovito dodaje, „u šumi kao partizani“. Prenosi i savjet jednog svećenika: ako ne daju moliti na trgu, neka po dvojica šeću trgom i mole, jer to im nitko ne može zabraniti. To je njihov intiman razgovor s Isusom, a „gdje su dvojica ili trojica sabrani u moje ime, ja sam tu“. Na taj se način, prema Grebenaru, na trgovima lome prokletstva zla o kojima je govorio u tumačenju.

Nakon završnog blagoslova voditelj podsjeća da se kupnjom prve, druge i treće knjige **„Isus lider“** pomaže dovršetak **Međunarodnog edukacijskog centra Kraljica Mira u Međugorju**. Riječ je o njegovu privatnom projektu u koji ulaže i osobni novac. Naglašava da ne gradi hotel ni restorane i da ne živi od turizma. Gradi prostor potreban za evangelizaciju, a „Bog zna zašto, pokazat će vrijeme“. Zahvaljuje svima koji su knjigu kupili s tom namjerom. Dodaje i da su se mnogi obratili čitajući „Isus lider“, bez obzira na to koji su dio čitali. Emisiju zatvara pozivom da se Ora et labora prati svaki dan, „na veću slavu Božju“.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na molitvu krunice, evangelizaciju i potporu prostoru namijenjenom navještaju vjere uglavnom je u skladu s katoličkom pobožnošću i misijskim poslanjem; crkveni izvori izričito potiču zajedničku molitvu krunice i njezinu povezanost s evangelizacijom i mirom. Izraz da se molitvom „lome prokletstva zla” traži pojašnjenje kako se ne bi shvatio kao obećanje da krunica djeluje automatski ili kao magijska tehnika.
concerns: „Lome prokletstva zla” može biti slikovit govor o duhovnoj borbi, ali ako se predstavlja kao zajamčen učinak određene molitve ili postupka, riskira praznovjeran ili magijski način razumijevanja molitve.

Savjet da se, ako molitva nije dopuštena na trgu, ondje moli u paru može biti mirno svjedočenje vjere, ali iz odlomka se ne može utvrditi pravni kontekst; katoličko svjedočenje ne treba shvatiti kao poziv na zaobilaženje zakonitih i razboritih ograničenja.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusove riječi o dvojici ili trojici sabranima u njegovo ime potvrđuju njegovu prisutnost među učenicima, a ne obećavaju da je svaka molitva određene skupine automatski učinkovitija ili da proizvodi zajamčen društveni učinak. Krunica je crkveno poticana pobožnost koja usmjerava vjernike prema Kristu i može podupirati evangelizaciju i mir, uz uvjet da se njezin smisao ne iskrivljuje. Samo financiranje edukacijskog centra kupnjom knjiga nije samo po sebi teološki problem; odlomak, međutim, ne daje dovoljno podataka za procjenu upravljanja projektom ili načina prikupljanja sredstava.

magisterium.assessment_en: The call to the prayer of the Rosary, evangelization, and support for a space intended for the proclamation of the faith is broadly in accordance with Catholic piety and missionary mandate; Church sources explicitly encourage the communal prayer of the Rosary and its connection with evangelization and peace. The expression that prayer "breaks the curses of evil" requires clarification so that it is not understood as a promise that the Rosary works automatically or as a magical technique.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' words about two or three gathered in his name confirm his presence among the disciples, rather than promising that every prayer of a particular group is automatically more efficacious or that it produces a guaranteed societal effect. The Rosary is a Church-encouraged devotion that directs believers toward Christ and can support evangelization and peace, provided that its meaning is not distorted. The financing of an educational center through the purchase of books is not in itself a theological issue; the passage, however, does not provide sufficient data to evaluate the management of the project or the method of fundraising.
concerns_en: "Breaking the curses of evil" may be figurative language about spiritual warfare, but if presented as a guaranteed effect of a specific prayer or procedure, it risks a superstitious or magical understanding of prayer.

The advice that, if prayer is not permitted in the square, one should pray there in pairs may be a peaceful witness of faith, but the legal context cannot be determined from the passage; Catholic witness should not be understood as a call to circumvent lawful and prudent restrictions.

sections.subtitle_en: Call to Men to the Squares, Blessing, and the Queen of Peace Center in Međugorje
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host calls men to the public prayer of the Rosary in the squares
sections.content_en:
Grebenar extends a call to **men from Germany and Austria** to the public prayer of the Rosary **in Zagreb on November 7**. He calls men in Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina to initiate the prayer of the Rosary in the square of their city or municipality. If they are not allowed to do so, let them pray next to the church or, as he humorously adds, "in the forest like partisans." He also conveys the advice of a priest: if they are not allowed to pray in the square, let them walk the square in pairs and pray, because no one can forbid them that. That is their intimate conversation with Jesus, and "where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I." In this way, according to Grebenar, the curses of evil about which he spoke in the interpretation are broken in the squares.

After the final blessing, the host reminds that by purchasing the first, second, and third books **"Jesus the Leader"** one helps the completion of the **Queen of Peace International Educational Center in Međugorje**. It is about his private project into which he also invests personal money. He emphasizes that he is not building a hotel or restaurants and that he does not live off tourism. He is building a space needed for evangelization, and "God knows why, time will tell." He thanks everyone who purchased the book with that intention. He also adds that many have converted reading "Jesus the Leader", regardless of which part they read. He closes the show with a call to follow Ora et labora every day, "for the greater glory of God."
